true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition overwrites the width/height API

Ruby does not overload by arity, so downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) on line 149 replaces downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) on line 145. The width/height wrapper never exists at runtime. Callers that still use the previous signature — numeric max width and max height, which this pull request does not update anywhere else — now bind the height integer to opts. optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] and raises NoMethodError instead of building a widthxheight geometry, so those calls 500.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client size check hardcoded to 10MB for every type

validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments each honored their admin setting. It now always uses 10 * 1024. Attachments larger than 10MB are rejected even when max_attachment_size_kb allows them, and attachments between the real attachment limit and 10MB pass the client and fail only on the server. Images are capped at 10MB regardless of max_image_size_kb, so a site that allows larger images cannot upload them from the browser. The 413 handler on line 246 uses the same hardcode, so the dialog always claims the limit is 10240 KB even when the web server or site setting differs.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
80% geometry breaks animation and does not enforce the size limit

The new call passes "80%" and allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails. When that setting is false, downsize_instructions runs convert with a [0] frame selector, so a large animated GIF or multi-page image is permanently flattened to the first frame in the stored original; that setting is about thumbnails, not the upload. When it is true, gifsicle --resize-fit is given "80%", but it requires a pixel size such as 100x100, so it exits non-zero. The failure is ignored, and after five attempts the still-oversized file is passed to Upload.create_for anyway. The loop also does not fail the upload if the file is still larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb after five 80% passes, so the comment's "reduced to allowed size" guarantee is not enforced for JPEGs or PNGs either.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
API URL downloads capped at a hardcoded 10MB for all types

FileHelper.download's limit changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to 10.megabytes for every upload type, not only images that will be downsized. Non-image API URL uploads are therefore cut off at 10MB even when max_attachment_size_kb is higher, and they are no longer tied to the attachment setting at all. Image URL uploads also cannot exceed 10MB when max_image_size_kb is configured above that, so the admin setting and the new downscale path disagree.

Downsize reads and writes the same tempfile

OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both source and destination. convert (and gifsicle when animation is enabled) opens the output for writing before the input is fully read, and ImageMagick truncates that path immediately. This tempfile is the only copy of the upload, so a large image can become empty or partial before Upload.create_for. The loop also ignores downsize's false return, so a failed conversion is retried against the already truncated file and then handed to create_for. Write to a separate tempfile and replace the original only after a successful non-empty result.

No input size ceiling before repeated ImageMagick runs

The browser and the URL-download path are capped at 10MB, but the multipart file branch never checks an upper bound before the downsize loop. The client check is bypassable: any logged-in user can POST a huge image and force up to five ImageMagick convert runs plus ImageOptim inside Scheduler::Defer. A decompression bomb or a multi-hundred-megabyte image is fully decoded on each attempt, which is a CPU and memory exhaustion path. Reject or cap the input before calling downsize, and stop if an attempt does not shrink the file.

No tests for downsizing or the new size caps

This change alters client limits, URL download limits, and runs a five-iteration ImageMagick downsize before Upload.create_for, but no tests were added. Failures such as in-place conversion, the overwritten downsize signature, attachment versus image limits, a file that stays over max_image_size_kb, and animated GIF handling would not be caught before merge.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Nil host crashes before validation

`before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` twice with no presence check. Create/update with a missing or null `embeddable_host[host]` (and any other save of a blank host) raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error, so the admin API returns 500 rather than the model's format error.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Update and destroy 500 when the id is missing

`update` and `destroy` load with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without a nil check. An unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns 500 instead of 404. `save_host` also assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` is present, so a malformed body 500s the same way.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host allow-list lookup ignores case and port

Lookup is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` using `URI#host` unchanged. The column side is lowercased but the bind value is not, so a referer host `Example.com` does not match a saved `example.com` under PostgreSQL. The format validator explicitly allows `:port`, and `before_validation` keeps it, but `URI#host` never includes the port, so a saved host `example.com:3000` never matches `http://example.com:3000/...`. Those referers are rejected by `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are interpolated raw and not normalized

Hosts are inserted with `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` and no normalization. A quote in a host aborts the migration (and is SQL injection if that setting was ever attacker-influenced). Protocol, path, and CR from the old newline list are stored as-is. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `URI#host` (e.g. `eviltrout.com`) to the stored string, so values the old setting accepted (`http://eviltrout.com`, `https://example.com/1234`) will not match after upgrade.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are interpolated raw and not normalized

Hosts are inserted with `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` and no normalization. A quote in a host aborts the migration (and is SQL injection if that setting was ever attacker-influenced). Protocol, path, and CR from the old newline list are stored as-is. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `URI#host` (e.g. `eviltrout.com`) to the stored string, so values the old setting accepted (`http://eviltrout.com`, `https://example.com/1234`) will not match after upgrade.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes unless embed_category matches a category name

The migration always runs `execute(... embed_category ...)[0]['id']`. Discourse only persists site settings that were overridden, and the join is `site_settings.value = categories.name`. On a normal install embed_category is absent or blank, the result set is empty, and `[0]` is nil, so the migration raises NoMethodError. PostgreSQL rolls the transaction back, so the upgrade cannot complete and embedding cannot be moved off the old setting.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

false_positives.candidate:
Existing allow-list is deleted and never copied

The copy of `embeddable_hosts` is gated on `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` after a SELECT. PG::Result#cmd_tuples is 0 for SELECT (row count is `ntuples`). The INSERT loop never runs, then the migration deletes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings. Any site that gets past the category lookup loses its allow-list and embedding starts rejecting every referer.

Hosts are not unique, so category assignment is arbitrary

There is no uniqueness validation and the migration adds no unique index on `host`. `record_for_host` uses `.first` with no order. Two rows for the same host (easy via the admin API, or a re-run of a fixed migration) make embed imports pick an arbitrary category, so "post to category" is not stable.

Import passes a category id through the name option

PostCreator is still called with `category:`, which previously received `SiteSetting.embed_category`, a category name (the migration joins that setting to `categories.name`). The new code passes `eh.try(:category_id)`, an integer. Nothing in this PR teaches PostCreator to treat that option as an id, so embedded topic creation will either raise or land in the uncategorized category instead of the host's chosen category. The new expectation in topic_embed_spec does not change PostCreator.

New embed admin API and migration are untested

The new controller specs only assert the class subclasses AdminController. They never hit create, update, destroy, a missing id, a blank host, or an unknown category. There is also no migration spec, so the empty `embed_category` crash, the `cmd_tuples` data loss, and un-normalized host inserts are not caught. `topic_spec`'s "embeddable_host is blank" example no longer stubs a host or an embed, so it does not lock the new `expandable_first_post?` behavior either.

Plural id hydration throws when the ids value is null

The new `*_ids` branch always calls `obj[k].map(...)` and only then does `hydrated || []`. A rest payload with a null or missing array for any `*_ids` key (not just embeddable hosts) throws TypeError inside `_hydrate` and fails the whole `find`/`findAll`. The `|| []` never runs for null, and the ids key is deleted only after the map.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing TopicUser crashes unsubscribe and the change is not recorded

TopicUser.find_by can return nil (user never had a topic_users row, or it was removed). The next line calls tu.notification_level and raises NoMethodError, so the unsubscribe link 500s instead of muting the topic. When a row does exist, tu.save! writes notification_level directly and skips TopicUser.change, so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at stay unset and no MessageBus notification_level_change is published. update_last_read auto-promotes to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and view time exceeds the auto-track threshold, which silently undoes the unsubscribe on a later visit. Other open tabs also keep the old level.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
No tests for per-topic unsubscribe behavior

The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into Email::MessageBuilder so the new %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation does not raise. Nothing asserts that the topic link is actually rendered, and there is no request/controller coverage for unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching vs regular vs muted transitions, a second request not changing the level again, slug redirect, or the login/CSRF constraints. The level rules are easy to get wrong and would regress silently.

Topic unsubscribe is a cookie-authenticated GET with no recipient token

Both unsubscribe routes are GET and TopicsController#unsubscribe mutates notification state with no CSRF token and no per-recipient key (unlike digest unsubscribe). Rails does not check authenticity tokens on GET, so a logged-in user's browser will apply the change for any third-party page that can trigger the URL (img, redirect, or link prefetch). The link is also not bound to the email recipient: whoever is logged in is the account that is changed, and a logged-out recipient is not unsubscribed until after a login round-trip.

Unsubscribe GET is not idempotent and does not stop topic emails

GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe changes notification_level on every request: tracking/watching (above regular) is set to regular, and regular or muted is set to muted. A watching user — the usual case for topic notification mail, including category auto-watch — is only dropped to regular, so reply, mention, quote, and category-watch emails continue, despite the email and page copy saying notifications for that topic will stop. Because the same transition runs again on refresh, prefetch, or a second click, that user is then muted. The action is also not safe to retry: there is no confirmation step and no check that the level was already updated.

Unsubscribe template will not resolve for the new route

The route is registered as a top-level topicUnsubscribe (/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe), and the route, controller, and view files are all named topic-unsubscribe, so Ember looks up the template topic-unsubscribe. This file is registered as topic/unsubscribe (the nested topic.unsubscribe name). Nothing sets templateName or renderTemplate, so the confirmation copy and the topic-notifications-button never render. After the Rails action mutates notification level, the user gets a missing-template error instead of the unsubscribe page. The Ember route also never calls an unsubscribe API itself, so a client-side transition to this URL would show the "you will stop receiving notifications" text without changing the level even if the template name were fixed.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Match stats are written inside validation and rolled back or double-counted

should_block? is invoked from EmailValidator during User validation, but it is not a pure check: it does match_count += 1, sets last_match_at, and calls save. User#save runs validations inside a transaction and raises ActiveRecord::Rollback when the user is invalid, so the counter update made while rejecting a blocked address is undone and never persisted on a normal save/save!/create. UsersController#create hides this for one path only: it calls user.valid? first (that increment commits) and then user.save (a second increment that rolls back), so the count is right there only by accident and any extra valid? double-counts. The same read-modify-write save also writes every column, so two concurrent matches can lose increments and a concurrent admin change to action_type can be overwritten. Match auditing is unreliable, and the new specs only call should_block? directly so they never catch the rollback.

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored

email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) after only escaping dots, then uses =~ with no end anchor or domain boundary. A whitelist value of company.com therefore matches user@company.com.attacker.example (and user@company.com.extra) as well as user@company.com, so a site that restricts signup to specific providers can be bypassed by any domain that merely contains the allowed domain as a substring. The same pattern makes a blacklist over-match unrelated hosts such as user@spam.com.legitimate.example. This is now the only server-side domain check (it was moved here from User), and nothing in the new specs covers whitelist or blacklist behavior.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email check is case- and whitespace-sensitive

BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the address with an exact BlockedEmail.where(email: email) match, and BlockedEmail only validates uniqueness of the raw email string (no downcasing or stripping in set_defaults). Signup stores whatever the user typed (User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] unchanged), while other paths such as change_email normalize with Email.downcase and strip. A blocked row for "bad@spam.com" therefore does not match "Bad@spam.com" or "bad@spam.com ", and the case-sensitive unique index will not treat those as the same address. Someone who was blocked can still register by changing case or surrounding whitespace.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Resize listener accepts any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl

The check is `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, i.e. accept when the sender origin is any substring of discourseUrl, not when it equals the forum origin. A shorter origin that is a prefix matches: if discourseUrl is `https://discuss.example.com`, a window at `https://discuss.example.co` has index 0 and is accepted. That page can postMessage a `discourse-resize` and set the iframe height arbitrarily (hide comments or stretch the frame over the host page). Compare parsed origins for equality, and require index 0 only if a prefix check is kept.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage targetOrigin is the full referer, so resize is dropped

The embed layout calls `parent.postMessage(..., request.referer)`. postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`), not a full URL with path and query. Browsers drop the message (or throw) when it does not match the parent origin. embed.js also sets the iframe to `scrolling=no` and only grows it on `discourse-resize`, so the comments frame stays at the default height and clips the discussion. Pass the referer origin only (and escape it for the JS string).

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
raw_html cook path stores and serves unsanitized HTML

Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, skipping PrettyText and Discourse's sanitizer. TopicEmbed.import persists RSS/Readability HTML with that cook method, and the embed view prints it with `raw post.cooked` (the main topic UI also treats cooked as HTML). PollFeed does `CGI.unescapeHTML` on feed content first, so entity-encoded markup becomes live tags, and Readability's allow-list still permits `javascript:`/`data:` href and src. Any feed item or fetched page can therefore plant stored XSS that runs for every forum visitor, not just inside the embed iframe. The imported-from footer makes this worse by interpolating the URL into an href with no escaping (`<a href='#{url}'>` in TopicEmbed.import), so a quote in an otherwise allowed http(s) URL breaks out of the attribute.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embed template has invalid ERB (`end if`)

`<%- end if %>` compiles to the Ruby statement `end if`, which is a SyntaxError. Rendering `/embed/best` when a topic already exists (the success path in EmbedController#best) will raise while compiling the template, so the iframe never shows highlights. It must be `<% end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed poll crashes unless every item has string content

`i.content.scrub` assumes every SimpleRSS item has a String `content`. RSS 2.0 items typically expose `description` and leave `content` nil; Atom can also omit it. Nil (or a non-string) raises NoMethodError, and because there is no rescue the hourly job aborts before later items are imported. `String#scrub` is also Ruby 2.1+ only, so this line fails on Ruby 2.0 even when content is present. Use description/content fallback and guard nil before unescaping.

false_negatives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

false_positives.candidate:
Disqus import drops category, original date, and offline permalinks

The importer no longer accepts `--category` and no longer passes `created_at` or `category` into topic creation. It now depends on `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which HTTP-fetches `t[:link]` and returns nil on any network/HTTP error. The following comment import is skipped entirely when that fetch fails, so a dead or blocked article URL drops the whole Disqus thread instead of creating the previous permalink stub. Category placement and original thread timestamps are also lost, and a single failed fetch aborts the rest of the file because nothing rescues `open`.

Embed controller spec expects a sync retrieve the action does not do

The 'no previous embed' example expects `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` during `get :best`. EmbedController#best only calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, so mocha fails this example and the job/throttle path is untested. The other success example renders `embed/best`, which currently raises SyntaxError on `end if`, so the `response.should be_success` after-hook fails as well. The spec will not pass as written and does not lock in the async behavior.

Unauthenticated embed URL fetch is an SSRF and topic-spam vector

import_remote uses `open(url).read` (open-uri) with no timeout, size limit, or redirect restriction. EmbedController#best is a public GET whose only gate is `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Referer is client-controlled, so any caller can spoof it and pass `embed_url` on the configured host. TopicRetriever then fetches that URL; open-uri follows redirects to arbitrary hosts (including link-local and cloud metadata). Each miss also enqueues RetrieveTopic with no controller-side dedupe, so unique URLs create unbounded jobs and, on success, topics posted as embed_by_username. open-uri is not even required from this file, so the fetch only works if some other file has already patched Kernel#open.

content_sha1 is advanced even when the post is not updated

On change, import always calls `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` after `revise!`, without checking that revise!/save succeeded. PostRevisor#revise! returns false when raw is unchanged and still returns true if `save` fails; either way the SHA is overwritten. The next poll then treats the feed item as already imported and never retries, so the topic body stays stale. If the linked post was deleted, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(post)` raises, which aborts the rest of the feed run. Update the SHA only after a successful save, and skip or recreate when the post is gone.

embed_url is varchar(255) but used as the unique lookup key

`t.string :embed_url` is a 255-character varchar, with a unique index on that column. TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed and import look up the full URL. Article and RSS links with tracking query strings routinely exceed 255 characters, so insert raises and the topic is never associated; truncated values would also collide or miss on lookup. Store embed_url as text (and index a hash if a unique constraint is still required).

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
box-ordinal-group is not shifted to the 1-based scale

@mixin order writes $val unchanged to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. Those 2009 properties are 1-based (initial value 1) and reject non-positive integers, while order, -webkit-order, and -ms-flex-order are 0-based (initial value 0). The equivalent legacy value is $val + 1. Today's call sites pass 2 and 3, so they still sort after items that omit order (legacy groups 1, 2, 3 versus modern 0, 2, 3) and the header does not mis-order yet. The shared mixin is still wrong for the model it claims to support: order(1) ties with unstyled siblings instead of following them, and order(0) is an invalid ordinal so the declaration is dropped and the item stays in the default group.

true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
2009 box display prefixes drop the header float fallback

flexbox() emits display: -webkit-box and display: -moz-box (and inline-flex() emits the inline equivalents) before the 2012 and unprefixed values. Engines that only implement the 2009 box model will honor that display and ignore later ones. That model does not pack with margin-left: auto and ignores float on children, but this PR removed .d-header .title { float: left } and .panel { float: right } and now depends on margin-left: auto to keep login and notification controls on the right. Those browsers therefore lay the logo and the panel out together at the start. Engines that understand none of the prefixed display values also lose the float fallback, so .panel becomes a normal full-width block under the logo. Either omit the 2009 display values and keep the floats as the non-flex fallback, or implement the matching -webkit-box-pack / -webkit-box-flex rules; the prefixes as written do not reproduce the layout they replaced.

false_negatives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

false_positives.candidate:
Header flex row overflows and pushes controls off-screen

.d-header .contents is now display: flex with the default flex-wrap: nowrap. .title, .extra-info-wrapper (only order: 2 in topic.scss), and .panel (only margin-left: auto and order: 3) never set min-width: 0, overflow: hidden, or flex-shrink: 0. Flex items default to min-width: auto, so they will not shrink below their content minimum, and margin-left: auto only eats positive free space — it does not stop overflow. A wide site logo (this file only sets #site-logo max-height: 40px, not a max-width) or a long docked topic title plus the 32px header icons therefore overflows the bar instead of ellipsizing or wrapping. On a narrow viewport the fixed header widens the page and login/notification controls are pushed out of view. The old float: left / float: right layout kept the panel shrink-to-fit on the right and let the middle content wrap inside the header width. Give the middle item flex: 1, min-width: 0, and overflow: hidden, and set flex-shrink: 0 on .title and .panel.

Small-action button float is ignored inside the new flex row

.small-action is now a flex container (flexbox() and align-items(center) at lines 264-265), but the action button is still placed with float: right. Float does not apply to flex items, and the patch never replaces it with margin-left: auto on the button or flex: 1 on .small-action-desc. For the usual short small-action label (closed, pinned, archived) in a wide post, the delete button therefore sits immediately after the text instead of at the right edge, which is where float: right put it. members used to render_serialized an array of GroupUserSerializer objects. It now returns an object {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}. The in-repo Group.findMembers caller was updated, but this is a public route. Themes, plugins, and API clients that treated the body as an array (for example result.map or a JSON array decode) will break or show no members. There is no compat path, such as keeping the array when limit/offset are omitted, or a versioned response.

Members limit and offset are unbounded and can 500

The rewritten members action uses limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset = params[:offset].to_i with no upper or lower bound. This route is available to anyone who can see the group, including public automatic groups that contain every user. A very large limit loads and serializes the entire membership in one request. A negative offset or limit is sent through to SQL; PostgreSQL rejects OFFSET/LIMIT < 0, so those query params 500 the endpoint. The old action at least defaulted automatic groups to 200; the rewrite should cap limit (and reject negative offset/limit) rather than trusting the client.

The audit-log endpoint always passes enable_advanced_features=True. The fallback branch (paginator.py:884-886) does the same for previous-page cursors. false_positives.candidate:
Eviction is not atomic with insert and can empty a segment

Span payloads are ZADDed in a separate non-transactional pipeline, and add-buffer.lua never receives the payload or score, so it cannot insert them. The 1000-span cap is a later ZPOPMIN using a count observed inside that script. Redis serializes each script, but two writers can both ZADD past the cap and both compute span_count-1000 from the pre-pop size. ProcessSpansStrategyFactory runs process_batch in a multiprocessing pool when num_processes != 1, and those workers share shards; rebalance/spillover can also double-write a trace. Two scripts that each see 2000 members will each pop 1000 and leave the segment empty. The old set-based union did not delete members on insert, so this data loss is new.

Hardcoded eviction can drop the root and the flush guard is gone

The cap is ZPOPMIN of span_count-1000 with a literal 1000. SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (default 1001) is no longer consulted, so that constructor argument does nothing. ZPOPMIN deletes the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores with no exception for the segment root, so a root that ended before a child (clock skew or a longer child) is discarded and the flushed segment has no root span. The flush-time check in _load_segment_data that skipped segments over max_segment_spans and emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded was removed, so if insert-time eviction does not run the consumer loads and publishes the whole segment up to the 10MiB byte limit. Evictions are not metered.

No tests for eviction, score order, or the new paginator

Buffer tests were only updated to supply end_timestamp_precise. Every case still uses four or five spans with the same timestamp, so CI never hits ZPOPMIN, never checks that the oldest spans are removed, never checks that the root is kept, and never covers WRONGTYPE on existing set keys or the concurrent double-pop race. The new audit-log OptimizedCursorPaginator path also has no test, so the datetime TypeError and the negative-offset ValueError would not fail CI.

Redirect walk cut from 10000 to 1000 splits deep traces

The parent-redirect loop now stops after 1000 hops, and the comment that this limit fails to join deep segment trees was removed. On a longer chain the loop exits at an intermediate span id, then HSET persists that partial redirect (span_id -> set_span_id). Later spans follow the truncated mapping, so the segment is permanently split and flushed as incomplete pieces. Child-first arrival stores one hop per ancestor, so a trace nested deeper than 1000 spans hits this. The previous cap was 10000 specifically because of that correctness limit.

Set-to-sorted-set switch breaks existing span-buffer keys

The buffer keys stay span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id, but the script and SpansBuffer now use ZADD, ZCARD, ZUNIONSTORE, ZSCAN, and ZPOPMIN. The previous code stored those keys as Redis SETs (SADD/SCARD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN). There is no new prefix, TYPE check, or migration. After deploy, every live segment is still a set until redis_ttl (default 3600s). ZADD or ZSCAN on it raises WRONGTYPE, process_spans fails, and the consumer retries the same batch for every in-flight trace. Flush fails the same way, so those segments are neither emitted nor deleted until the key expires.

ZUNIONSTORE SUM and self-union UNLINK drop or mis-rank spans

Merges use ZUNIONSTORE with the default AGGREGATE SUM. A member present in both inputs (Kafka redelivery, or the same payload written to both the parent key and a child key) gets its end-timestamp scores added, so it sorts as far in the future and ZPOPMIN evicts other spans instead. If the resolved set id equals the current span id, span_key and set_key are the same key: the script unions the key with itself and then UNLINK span_key, deleting the destination the preceding ZADD just wrote. That hits a non-root span whose parent_span_id equals its span_id, or whose redirect chain resolves to its own id. Those spans are gone before flush.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Eligibility cache key uses process-randomized hash() and cannot be invalidated

The cache key is error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}. Python hash() is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so workers do not share keys, invalidate_upsampling_cache deletes a different key than other processes wrote, and nothing in this PR calls that invalidator when the allowlist changes anyway. A collision of two project-id tuples in one process also serves the wrong eligibility for 60 seconds and rewrites count() for projects that are not fully allowlisted. Use a stable key (for example a sorted, joined id list) and hook invalidation to allowlist updates, or drop the cache; options.get is already an in-process read.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling decision ignores the dataset and query actually executed

_get_event_stats decides upsampling from the closed-over request dataset and request.GET, not from scoped_dataset or the query argument. Dashboard widget splitting calls this helper with a different dataset and rewritten queries (errors-only "!event.type:transaction", transactions-only "event.type:transaction", and the original metrics dataset). A metrics/discover split therefore either skips upsampling on the errors subquery (outer dataset is not errors/discover) or, when the original request string looks like an error query, applies sum(sample_weight) to the transactions-only probe. Split detection uses those counts (has_errors / has_transactions), so widget discoverSplitDecision can be saved incorrectly, and transaction probes can throw if sample_weight is absent. The eligibility check has to use the dataset and query string passed into this call.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

false_positives.candidate:
Accidental gitlink committed at the PR base commit

This change adds sentry-repo as a gitlink/submodule pointer to a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a (the PR base) with no .gitmodules entry and no relation to upsampling. Clones and CI that recurse into submodules, or tools that refuse gitlinks, will fail or nest a second checkout of this repo. The gitlink should be removed before merge.

Allowlist option is never registered and is read on every stats query

Every events-stats execution calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, which on a cache miss calls options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", []). This PR never registers that option (no defaults.py or options change). Sentry's options manager raises UnknownOption for unregistered keys even when a default is passed, so a cache miss 500s the whole organization events-stats endpoint, including non-error datasets and projects that should not be upsampled. If a deployment's options.get instead returns the default, the feature never turns on in production; the new tests hide that by mocking options. The lookup also does `project_id in allowlist` with no int/str normalization, so a JSON allowlist of string ids never matches int project ids (feature silently off), and a non-list value raises TypeError on this same hot path.

Error detection is a substring match and treats negated filters as errors

_is_error_focused_query lowercases the raw query and returns True if it contains the substring "event.type:error". That matches !event.type:error, !(event.type:error), event.type:error OR event.type:transaction, and the token as a prefix of a longer value or inside a message/tag search. For discover queries on allowlisted projects, count() is then rewritten to sum(sample_weight) even when the query is explicitly not errors. Transaction and other non-error events do not have a reliable sample_weight, so those stats queries either error or return zeros/inflated mixed counts. A search parser check for a positive event.type:error condition is required; substring matching is the opposite of the stated caution.

Errors dataset always upsamples, but upsampled_count is only registered on discover

_should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True for the errors snuba dataset with no query check, and the endpoint then rewrites count() to upsampled_count(). The new aggregate is added only to the discover dataset function_converter in this PR. Errors timeseries uses its own query builder/config; if that config does not inherit this converter, allowlisted dataset=errors count() requests fail with an unknown function. The new snuba tests never pass dataset=errors (they rely on discover plus event.type:error), so this path is untested and can 400/500 the errors stats API.

Every events-stats query now takes a remote cache round trip

is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects always cache.get's before it knows the dataset is errors. That helper runs on every _get_event_stats call, including transaction, span, and metrics queries, and dashboard split runs it several times per request. options.get of the allowlist is already served from the in-process options cache; this adds a shared-cache RTT (and a hard dependency on that cache) on the events-stats hot path to avoid a cheaper lookup. A slow or failing cache delays or fails unrelated stats requests. The allowlist check should happen only after the dataset/query gate, and should not require a remote cache.

Top-events ranking still uses raw count() while the series is rewritten

For topEvents, only the timeseries y-axis list is passed through transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling. orderby still comes from get_orderby(request) and selected_columns from get_field_list, on both the RPC path (orderby around line 241) and top_events_timeseries (orderby around line 259). A request ordered by count() or -count() therefore ranks the top N groups by the sampled count while the returned series uses upsampled_count. Callers get the wrong groups, or the top-N query fails if it also references the rewritten alias. orderby and any count() in the top-N selected columns need the same transform as the timeseries columns.

Upsampled count sums sample_weight, but nothing stores the inverse sample rate

upsampled_count is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no ifNull/coalesce. The only write-path change is the test factory, which copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate onto sample_rate (the rate itself, e.g. 0.1), not sample_weight, and production ingest is not updated at all. Events therefore have no sample_weight. ClickHouse sum of nulls is 0, so once the rewrite runs, allowlisted error counts become 0 instead of the real count or 1/sample_rate. That also cannot satisfy the new stats test, which stores client_sample_rate 0.1 and expects count == 10. toInt64 additionally truncates any fractional weight. Historical events and transactions that lack the column are zeroed or fail the query rather than falling back to count().

count() is rewritten to a column string the field parser will not accept

When upsampling is enabled, count() is replaced with the literal "upsampled_count() as count" and passed as a selected column / y-axis. Sentry's field parser treats a column as a function only when the string ends with ')'; this value does not, so it is resolved as a raw column name rather than the new upsampled_count aggregate. Allowlisted error count() stats queries then fail field validation (or, if an alias were accepted, the result key would not stay the `count` field the events-stats contract and the new test expect). Charts, top-events, and any client requesting yAxis=count() for an allowlisted project break instead of returning an upsampled series.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Error context is paired by dict value order, not node id

fetch_error_details loads nodestore blobs with get_multi(node_ids) and then zips error_ids with events.values(). get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id; value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, and backends that omit missing keys shift every subsequent pair. The summary sent to Seer can attribute the wrong title, message, and timestamp to an error id, or drop the wrong events via the data is not None filter. Lookups need to be events.get(node_id) for each id. Timestamps are also used raw in gen_request_data comparisons; a non-numeric nodestore timestamp (ISO string) raises TypeError and fails the whole summarize request.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Flagged table widgets render an empty table instead of query results

When organization feature use-table-widget-visualization is on, WidgetCardChart renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData hardcoded to data: [] and empty meta, ignoring result.data, result.meta, fields, loading, and the dataset field renderer. Dashboard table widgets for that org show a blank grid instead of the widget query. columns={[]} also does not fall back to meta.fields, because TableWidgetVisualization uses columns ?? derivedColumns and an empty array is not nullish.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Age/timestamp mutual exclusion treats 0 as absent

validate_timestamp and validate_age use initial_data.get('age') and initial_data.get('timestamp') as booleans. Reporting API age of 0 (report just generated) and timestamp of 0 are valid integers allowed by the field constraints, but both are falsy, so a report that includes both is accepted. Neither field is required, so a report with neither age nor timestamp also passes even though each spec needs one of them.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
60s deadline is too short for a 100-identity SSO refresh batch

check_auth_identities now has processing_deadline_duration=60 while check_auth still hands it up to chunk_size (100) identities. Each identity can do an external IdP refresh. check_auth stamps last_synced before enqueueing this task, so if the worker kills the task at 60s the remaining identities are not refreshed and will not be selected again until the next AUTH_CHECK_INTERVAL (about a day). SSO validity checks are skipped for the tail of every oversized batch.

AI summary treats an unloaded project as missing

Project is resolved with useProjectFromId({project_id: replayRecord?.project_id}), which is undefined both while the project list is still loading and when the project truly does not exist. The new branch returns 'Project not found' whenever project_id is set and project is missing, before the isPending check, and the summarize query stays disabled. Users hit a hard error (at least a flash, or a stuck error if projects never include that id yet) instead of waiting for the project store.

Attribute key hook returns undefined after a failed fetch

The old hook always reduced the response into a TagCollection, so a failed request still yielded {}. The new hook returns useQuery data directly (attributes: isFetching ? previous : data) and dropped retry: false. On error, data is undefined and isFetching is false, so attributes becomes undefined. Explore callers that spread or index attributes (string tags, number tags, has-tag) will throw when the trace-item attributes endpoint fails. Default react-query retry (3) and refetchOnWindowFocus also replace the previous retry: false and refetchOnWindowFocus: false, multiplying load on that endpoint.

Feedback list no longer fills the grid cell and will not scroll

The list grid area used to be a FluidHeight Container, which constrained height and scrolled the list inside the 1fr row. It is now SummaryListContainer, a flex column with no min-height: 0, overflow: hidden, or height: 100%. Grid items default to min-height: auto, so the column grows with the summary plus the full list instead of staying in the viewport row, and the inner FluidHeight percentage height does not resolve to the leftover space. The feedback list scroll pane breaks once the summary is shown.

Feedback summary ignores environment (and search) page filters

useFeedbackSummary requests /feedback-summary/ with only the normalized datetime and selection.projects. The feedback list page is scoped by the page-filter environment selection (and the search box), but those are not sent. With an environment selected, the Seer summary describes all environments in the projects while the list shows one environment, so the summary does not match the data on screen.

Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching

HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the search filter branch. When searchQuery is empty the function returns sortAttributes(attributes) immediately, so those internal fields stay visible in the default attributes tree. They disappear only after the user types a query, including when the query would otherwise match them. The exclusion needs to run before the early return.

Issue titles are interpolated into markdown links unsanitized

MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE places the issue title inside a markdown link label: [**{title}**]({url}). Issue titles are attacker-controlled error text and are only length-truncated, not escaped. A title containing ](https://evil.example) or a newline closes the link early and can inject extra markdown into the comment the Sentry bot posts on the customer's GitHub/GitLab PR. Environment names are likewise dropped into the comment in backticks with no escaping.

Replay error lookup depends on date filters the client never sends

Every summarize request now calls get_filter_params and query_replay_instance before building logs, and process_raw_response is given request.query_params.getlist('field'). The replay AI tab requests /summarize/breadcrumbs/ with no start, end, statsPeriod, or field=error_ids. If get_filter_params rejects a missing range, the previously working summary 400s. If it defaults to a recent window, error_ids is empty for replays outside that window, so error context is silently omitted. A Snuba failure also 500s a path that previously only needed recording segments. error_ids must be requested explicitly and the replay's own time range used, not the caller's page filters.

Suspect-issue PR comments call methods that do not exist on the workflow

get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, not on PRCommentWorkflow. PRCommentWorkflow is a separate workflow type that holds an integration; it does not gain that staticmethod. GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body also call self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and self.get_environment_info, which were added only on CommitContextIntegration. Generating a merged-PR suspect-issue comment therefore raises AttributeError and the GitHub/GitLab comment workflow fails instead of posting.

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code match does not normalize case or whitespace

Stored codes are lowercase hex from `randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, shown as `xxxxx-xxxxx`. Login and disable only do `replaceAll("-", "")` and then `indexOf`, so they are case-sensitive and do not trim. The backup-code input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which tells users to type uppercase. A code typed that way, or pasted with a trailing newline or space from the downloaded file, does not match and is rejected as incorrect even though it is the right code. The same comparison is in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` around the `replaceAll` call, so disable has the same failure.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Consuming a backup code is a lost update

A valid backup code is invalidated by reading the decrypted list, setting that index to null, and writing the whole blob back with a plain `user.update`. There is no transaction, row lock, or compare-and-swap on the previous ciphertext. Two overlapping logins (double submit, retry, or two devices) both read the same list. If they use the same code, both pass `indexOf` before either write and both sessions are created, so the code is not single-use. If they use different codes, the later write restores the code the earlier request nulled, so a spent code works again. Consumption needs to be serialized, for example by locking the user row and updating only if `backupCodes` is still the value that was read.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup code login can skip the password

Password verification only runs when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode`. The new branch then accepts a backup code whenever `credentials.backupCode` is non-empty and never checks the password itself. The login UI clears `totpCode` before submitting a backup code so the password gate runs, but the credentials callback does not enforce that pairing. A caller who knows a backup code can send the victim's email, any non-empty `totpCode`, and that backup code and receive a session without the password. Backup codes are long-lived and typically stored in a downloaded text file, so this makes them a single factor rather than a replacement for the authenticator. Disable 2FA already requires the password independently of the second factor; login should do the same before accepting a backup code.

Backup-code download click does not reliably download

The download action is a `<Button>` nested inside `<a download href={backupCodesUrl}>`, which is invalid HTML (interactive content inside an anchor). The button handles the click, so the anchor's download navigation often never runs and `cal-backup-codes.txt` is not saved. Unlike the Copy and Close buttons in the same footer, this control also does not call `preventDefault`. It sits inside the enable `<Form>`, so if the button submits, the click re-invokes `handleEnable` with the already-used TOTP code instead of downloading. The new e2e test waits on a download from that test id and will fail or flake for the same reason.

Copy toast reports success even when clipboard write fails

`navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` is not awaited and has no catch, and `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` runs immediately. `writeText` rejects when clipboard permission is denied or the page is not allowed to write the clipboard, which is common in embedded or non-secure contexts. The user is told the codes were copied, then Close is the path that finishes setup. Because codes cannot be fetched again after 2FA is enabled, a failed copy plus close leaves them with no saved codes. The e2e test only waits for `toast-success`, so it passes even when nothing was copied.

Dismissing the codes dialog loses the only copy

After TOTP enable succeeds, the modal only advances to DisplayBackupCodes; `onEnable()` runs solely from the Close button. The dialog is still closed through `onOpenChange` (Escape, overlay, header close), which does not call `onEnable()` or `resetState()`. Codes are returned once from setup and kept only in component state. Setup refuses to run again once `twoFactorEnabled` is true, and nothing in this PR can list or regenerate them. Dismissing the dialog therefore drops the only display of the codes and can leave the settings page thinking 2FA is still off, so a later enable attempt hits TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled. The new `missing_backup_codes` string says to generate codes in settings, but no such screen exists, including for users who enabled 2FA before this column was added and have null `backupCodes`.

OAuth/SAML second-factor screen cannot use backup codes

Lost access is only rendered in `TwoFactorFooter`. When login is reached with a `totp` query JWT (`totpEmail` set), the footer is `ExternalTotpFooter`, which is only Cancel, so those users never see the backup-code field. That is the path `loginWithTotp` uses after Google/SAML sign-in for an account with `twoFactorEnabled` (including CAL users whose password was cleared when the identity provider was linked). Even a direct credentials call with only a backup code fails first: `authorize` throws `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` when `identityProvider !== CAL` and `totpCode` is empty, before the backup-code branch. Those users still cannot get in with a backup code if they lose the authenticator.

Tests never log in with a backup code, and enable flow is unfinished

The new step shows backup codes and does not call `onEnable()` until Close, but the "enable 2FA and login using 2FA" test never clicks `backup-codes-close`. It still asserts the switch via `locator.isChecked()`, which this PR notes passes even when the switch is not checked, so the test can stay green if the post-enable UI never updates. The other test only checks download filename, a success toast, and close. Nothing submits a backup code at login, checks that a used code is rejected, or disables 2FA with a backup code. The file's own TODO calls that out, and the PR checklist says tests that prove the feature were not added. The password-skip and single-use bugs above would not be caught.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty

create() now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. If location is Google Meet and destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or [], mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and this throws TypeError before any video or calendar event is created, so the booking request fails. Previously `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` was used, which fell back to Cal Video instead of crashing. The same check only looks at index 0, so a collective event whose first destination is not Google Calendar is forced off Meet even when a later destination is Google.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google update/delete fallback can never resolve a calendar id

updateEvent and deleteEvent now do `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is null or omitted, the find compares every calendar to that same falsy value and never matches, so selectedCalendar/calendarId is undefined. Previously this fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId. updateEvent then calls Google with calendarId undefined and the reschedule/update fails; deleteEvent falls through to "primary" and leaves the event on a non-primary calendar. CalendarManager.deleteEvent still calls deleteEvent(uid, event) without an external id, and any booking reference with a null externalCalendarId hits this path. The hangout description patch in createEvent also uses selectedCalendar with no "primary" fallback after insert used `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, so a Meet event written to primary never gets the hangout link written back.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug assignment condition was inverted

Unrelated to destination calendars, the org create payload changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Previously a slug was written when team billing was disabled, and only requestedSlug was stored when billing was enabled. Now billing-disabled instances create organizations with no slug (org URLs break), and billing-enabled instances set slug immediately as well as requestedSlug, skipping the flow that waits to assign the slug. The requestedSlug ternary next to it is behavior-preserving; the slug line dropped the negation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateAllCalendarEvents calls updateEvent with a missing credential

When a calendar reference has a credentialId that is not on the EventManager user, the code loads it from the DB, but if that lookup misses (deleted credential, or app.slug absent so the rebuild is skipped) it still pushes updateEvent(credential, ...) with credential undefined. getCalendar then throws on credential.type. That rejection fails Promise.all for every calendar reference in the batch, and the catch returns synthetic failures and no longer console.errors the message it builds, so a reschedule/location update can report total failure after partially applying. createAllCalendarEvents correctly skips a missing credential; this path does not.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancelling remaining recurring bookings does not delete each host calendar event

The new per-reference loop wraps the recurring allRemainingBookings branch unchanged. For every calendar reference that has a credentialId, that branch ignores the reference just fetched and instead walks every organizer calendar credential and, for each remaining instance, references.find() of the first _calendar ref only, then deleteEvent on that uid. Co-host references are never selected, so their recurring events stay on the calendar. The same first event is deleted once per outer reference times every organizer calendar credential, and the credential loaded for the current reference is unused. Non-recurring cancel correctly deletes each reference with its own credential; recurring cancel does not.

Collective co-host calendars dropped when organizer has none

evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when both eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar are missing, and the collective branch then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). Optional push on null is a no-op, so every co-host destination calendar collected above is discarded. createAllCalendarEvents then takes the empty/null path and its fallback filters credentials with type === "calendar", which never matches google_calendar/office365_calendar/etc. A collective booking whose first host has no destination calendar creates no host calendar events at all, which is the case this PR is meant to fix.

Last calendar result overwrites evt.iCalUID

While building references, every calendar result assigns evt.iCalUID = result.iCalUID. createAllCalendarEvents now returns one result per host calendar, and each Google insert has its own iCalUID. The assignment keeps only the last host's UID on the shared event object that callers use for confirmation emails and ICS. Attendee clients can then fail to match the organizer's event. The UID is also not fed into later createEvent calls, so the host events are not correlated with each other either.

No test covers multi-host destination calendars

The PR checklist says no tests were added. Nothing covers createAllCalendarEvents with two destination calendars, the Google Meet empty-array crash, co-host calendars when the organizer destination is null, video reference credentialId, recurring cancel of multiple calendar references, or the webhook payload shape. The only e2e edit changes BOOKING_REJECTED destinationCalendar from null to [] and would not catch these regressions.

Only the first destination calendar is stored on the booking

The booking create connects only evt.destinationCalendar[0]. Booking.destinationCalendar is a single relation, and confirm.handler, the Stripe and PayPal payment webhooks, edit location, and the booking reminder all rebuild CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar from that one row (or the organizer user row) wrapped in an array. Those paths call EventManager.create/update. Collective bookings that defer calendar creation until confirmation or payment therefore never see co-host destination calendars, so only the organizer gets a calendar event. The in-memory array built for the initial request is not recoverable later.

Per-host calendar create still uses only the first destination

createAllCalendarEvents loops every destination and calls createEvent with that destination's credential, but it passes the full event whose destinationCalendar array still starts with the organizer. Office 365 (CalendarService.ts createEvent around the eventsUrl built from destinationCalendar[0]), Lark (calendarId from destinationCalendar[0]), and CalDAV (BaseCalendarService filters to destinationCalendar[0].externalId) therefore run host 2's token against host 1's calendar id. Graph/Lark return 404 or throw, and CalDAV's filter can match nothing yet still return a successful NewCalendarEventType, so a booking reference is stored for an event that was never created. Google insert does look up by credentialId, but the organizer attendee email is still destinationCalendar[0].externalId (Google CalendarService.ts around the mainHostDestinationCalendar email), so a co-host event is created with another host marked organizer:true and Google can reject the insert. The no-credentialId branch (createEvent without externalId) never matches that lookup and silently writes to the Google primary calendar instead of the configured externalId, and can do so once per credential of that integration.

Request-reschedule does not delete co-host calendar events

Calendar cleanup builds credentialsMap from getUsersCredentials(user.id) keyed only by credential.type, then deleteEvent uses credentialsMap.get(bookingRef.type). Collective bookings now have one calendar reference per host, often the same type (google_calendar) but different credentialIds. The map keeps a single credential for that type, and co-host credential ids on the references are ignored, so co-host events are deleted with the requesting user's token (Google 404) and remain on the co-host calendar. handleCancelBooking was updated to load credentialId from the DB; this path was not.

Seat-merge reschedule deletes only one old calendar event

When newBookingId is set, updateAllCalendarEvents still does booking.references.find() for a single _calendar reference and deletes only that uid. Collective bookings now store one calendar reference per host. Merging a seated booking onto an existing slot therefore removes one host's old event and leaves the other hosts' events at the old time.

Video booking references no longer store credentialId

In create(), referencesToCreate now sets credentialId only for calendar results (`isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`). Video results previously kept result.credentialId. handleCancelBooking deletes the meeting only when bookingVideoReference.credentialId is set and looks that credential up; with credentialId always omitted, cancelling a new booking never calls deleteMeeting, so Zoom/Daily/Meet links stay live after cancel. updateLocation() still copies result.credentialId, so only the initial create path is broken.

Webhook destinationCalendar shape is a breaking, inconsistent change

CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a single DestinationCalendar | null to an array, and that object is spread into BOOKING_CREATED / BOOKING_CANCELLED / BOOKING_REJECTED webhook payloads. Consumers reading payload.destinationCalendar.externalId or .integration will break; the PR is marked non-breaking and does not version the payload. Emitters also disagree on the empty value: handleNewBooking still assigns null, while confirm, cancel, payment webhooks, and the rejected webhook e2e expectation use []. BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED tests still expect null, so clients cannot rely on one empty shape either.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Absent refresh_token is overwritten with the literal string "refresh_token"

After a successful parse, if refresh_token is missing or empty the helper sets it to the string "refresh_token". Office365CalendarService then spreads tokenResponse.data onto the saved credential. Microsoft's refresh response often omits refresh_token (the Office 365 schema marks it optional, and the previous safeParse path left the stored token untouched). The real refresh token is replaced, the next refresh sends refresh_token=refresh_token, and Microsoft returns invalid_grant, permanently disconnecting Outlook calendar. This runs whether or not credential sync is enabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync-mode token schema cannot match any real token payload

minimumTokenResponseSchema is a z.object whose extra keys are the literal strings produced by z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() (Zod type names / "[object Object]"), not wildcards, and the object is not passthrough. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, every refresh goes through this schema. Real bodies only have access_token and an expiry field, so safeParse always fails and the helper throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Google, Office 365, Zoom, and Salesforce token refresh cannot succeed in sync mode, and the comment's intent (treat any numeric field as expiry and keep other properties) is not implemented.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google refresh writes the Zod result wrapper into credential.key

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod SafeParse object ({ success, data }), not the parsed credential. GoogleCalendarService assigns that return value straight to key and prisma.credential.update persists it. This runs on every access-token refresh even when credential sync is disabled (the old code stored googleCredentialSchema.parse(...), which returned the credential itself). After the first refresh the row is no longer a Google credential, so the next GoogleCalendarService constructor throws in googleCredentialSchema.parse and Google Calendar stops working until the user reconnects.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync refresh returns a raw Fetch Response that callers do not understand

When credential sync is on, refreshOAuthTokens returns the Fetch Response and never checks response.ok or reads response.json(). Callers were not updated to that contract: Google reads res.data (gaxios), HubSpot treats the result as a HubspotToken (accessToken/expiresIn), Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read axios .data and persist it, and Lark passes the body to handleLarkError which expects Lark's { code, data } envelope. A sync response of { access_token, expiry } therefore throws or is written into credential.key as the wrong shape. Non-2xx responses are also treated as success. Turning on the new env vars breaks token refresh for those apps instead of delegating it.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

A sync response of { access_token, expiry } therefore throws or is written into credential.key as the wrong shape. Non-2xx responses are also treated as success. Turning on the new env vars breaks token refresh for those apps instead of delegating it.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Zoho Bigin passes credential id where the sync API expects user id

refreshOAuthTokens' third argument is the Cal.com user id (sent as calcomUserId). BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken passes credentialId instead. With sync enabled, the parent app looks up the wrong user and can return that user's access token; the following code persists tokenInfo.data onto this credential. Even before response parsing is fixed, the parent is asked to mint or rotate tokens for an unrelated id. Other adapters pass credential.userId.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Salesforce refresh calls prisma without an import and then uses the old access token

getClient now always refreshes the Salesforce token and calls prisma.credential.update, but this file never imports prisma. Constructing SalesforceCalendarService therefore throws ReferenceError before any Event/Contact call, so the Salesforce integration is broken for every user, not only credential-sync deployments.
