There is no uniqueness validation and the migration adds no unique index on `host`. `record_for_host` uses `.first` with no order. Two rows for the same host (easy via the admin API, or a re-run of a fixed migration) make embed imports pick an arbitrary category, so "post to category" is not stable.

The new `*_ids` branch always calls `obj[k].map(...)` and only then does `hydrated || []`. The new controller specs only assert the class subclasses AdminController. They never hit create, update, destroy, a missing id, a blank host, or an unknown category. false_positives.candidate:
Public group members page only loads the first 50 users

setupController always calls Group.findMembers(), and that method now always requests limit 50 (the new model default) and offset 0. The public members template (group/members.hbs) only iterates `members` and has no next/previous controls, unlike the admin group screen. Previously this endpoint returned every member of a non-automatic group and defaulted automatic groups to 200 when no limit was sent. After this change, any group with more than 50 members (including large custom groups and automatic groups such as trust_level_0) silently hides everyone past the first page, with no way to load the rest.

Removing the last member on a page leaves a blank page

findMembers clamps the request offset with Math.min(user_count, offset) using the in-memory user_count, which is only refreshed from the response. removeMember (and addMembers) then call findMembers() without moving offset back. Deleting the last user on the current page therefore re-requests an offset that is now past the end (the clamp still allows offset == old total). The server echoes that offset in meta and returns an empty members array, and the client stores meta.offset, so the admin UI stays on a blank page until Previous is clicked. The members action never clamps offset to the last non-empty page either.

Remove control ignores whether the group is automatic

This row is rendered by the group-member itemView, not in the admin group template's context. Ember's each+itemView sets the row context to the each keyword ({member: user}) or to the user record; neither has the group's automatic flag, and a replaced context does not fall back to the admin-group controller. {{#unless automatic}} is therefore always true, so the remove link is shown for automatic groups (admins, moderators, trust_level_*, and so on). Confirming still calls DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members, which correctly returns 422, but neither the removeMember action nor Group.removeMember handles the failure, so the admin gets a confirm dialog and then no error and no list refresh.

Creating a group drops the chosen alias level

create assigns name and visible, then saves, but never reads params[:alias_level]. The admin form shows the alias-level combo for new groups (it sits outside the {{#if id}} block), and Group.asJSON posts alias_level on create. update does apply alias_level, so editing an existing group works, but the first save always persists the default (0, nobody) no matter what was selected. The client only copies resp.basic_group.id back onto the model, so the UI keeps showing the unsaved choice until the group is reloaded. The new create spec only checks name stripping and would not catch this.

Members limit and offset are unbounded and can 500

The rewritten members action uses limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset = params[:offset].to_i with no upper or lower bound. This route is available to anyone who can see the group, including public automatic groups that contain every user. A very large limit loads and serializes the entire membership in one request. A negative offset or limit is sent through to SQL; PostgreSQL rejects OFFSET/LIMIT < 0, so those query params 500 the endpoint. The old action at least defaulted automatic groups to 200; the rewrite should cap limit (and reject negative offset/limit) rather than trusting the client.

GET /groups/:name/members.json response shape changed

members used to render_serialized an array of GroupUserSerializer objects. It now returns an object {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}. The in-repo Group.findMembers caller was updated, but this is a public route. Themes, plugins, and API clients that treated the body as an array (for example result.map or a JSON array decode) will break or show no members. There is no compat path, such as keeping the array when limit/offset are omitted, or a versioned response.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Match stats are written inside validation and rolled back or double-counted

should_block? is invoked from EmailValidator during User validation, but it is not a pure check: it does match_count += 1, sets last_match_at, and calls save. User#save runs validations inside a transaction and raises ActiveRecord::Rollback when the user is invalid, so the counter update made while rejecting a blocked address is undone and never persisted on a normal save/save!/create. UsersController#create hides this for one path only: it calls user.valid? first (that increment commits) and then user.save (a second increment that rolls back), so the count is right there only by accident and any extra valid? double-counts. The same read-modify-write save also writes every column, so two concurrent matches can lose increments and a concurrent admin change to action_type can be overwritten. Match auditing is unreliable, and the new specs only call should_block? directly so they never catch the rollback.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same underlying issue: a blocking-check method updates match statistics and saves records during a read/validation operation. It also explicitly describes concurrent lost updates, matching the golden comment's race-condition concern. The additional rollback and double-counting details do not change the core match.

Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored

A whitelist value of company.com therefore matches user@company.com.attacker.example (and user@company.com.extra) as well as user@company.com, so a site that restricts signup to specific providers can be bypassed by any domain that merely contains the allowed domain as a substring. The same pattern makes a blacklist over-match unrelated hosts such as user@spam.com.legitimate.example. This is now the only server-side domain check (it was moved here from User), and nothing in the new specs covers whitelist or blacklist behavior.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same unanchored domain regex in email_in_restriction_setting?, which permits whitelist bypasses through partial domain matches. The candidate uses a different malicious-domain example but describes the same missing domain-boundary anchoring issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the address with an exact BlockedEmail.where(email: email) match, and BlockedEmail only validates uniqueness of the raw email string (no downcasing or stripping in set_defaults). true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
2009 box display prefixes drop the header float fallback

flexbox() emits display: -webkit-box and display: -moz-box (and inline-flex() emits the inline equivalents) before the 2012 and unprefixed values. Engines that only implement the 2009 box model will honor that display and ignore later ones. That model does not pack with margin-left: auto and ignores float on children, but this PR removed .d-header .title { float: left } and .panel { float: right } and now depends on margin-left: auto to keep login and notification controls on the right. Those browsers therefore lay the logo and the panel out together at the start. Engines that understand none of the prefixed display values also lose the float fallback, so .panel becomes a normal full-width block under the logo. Either omit the 2009 display values and keep the floats as the non-flex fallback, or implement the matching -webkit-box-pack / -webkit-box-flex rules; the prefixes as written do not reproduce the layout they replaced.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify removal of the header panel's float-right fallback as causing loss of right alignment and potentially stacking the panel beneath the title in non-flex layouts. The candidate adds legacy flexbox compatibility concerns and does not explicitly name the noscript header, but captures the same underlying layout regression.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
box-ordinal-group is not shifted to the 1-based scale

@mixin order writes $val unchanged to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. Those 2009 properties are 1-based (initial value 1) and reject non-positive integers, while order, -webkit-order, and -ms-flex-order are 0-based (initial value 0). The equivalent legacy value is $val + 1. Today's call sites pass 2 and 3, so they still sort after items that omit order (legacy groups 1, 2, 3 versus modern 0, 2, 3) and the header does not mis-order yet. The shared mixin is still wrong for the model it claims to support: order(1) ties with unstyled siblings instead of following them, and order(0) is an invalid ordinal so the declaration is dropped and the item stays in the default group.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify that the legacy -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group properties require 1-based values, but the mixin passes $val unchanged, making 0 invalid and potentially causing incorrect layout in older browsers.

Small-action button float is ignored inside the new flex row

.small-action is now a flex container (flexbox() and align-items(center) at lines 264-265), but the action button is still placed with float: right. Float does not apply to flex items, and the patch never replaces it with margin-left: auto on the button or flex: 1 on .small-action-desc. For the usual short small-action label (closed, pinned, archived) in a wide post, the delete button therefore sits immediately after the text instead of at the right edge, which is where float: right put it. The description's old padding (0.5em 0 0.5em 4em) that cleared the 45px floated avatar was also reduced to 0 1.5%, so any browser that ignores every display value emitted by flexbox() still honors float: left on .topic-avatar and draws the label underneath that icon.

.d-header .contents is now display: flex with the default flex-wrap: nowrap. .title, .extra-info-wrapper (only order: 2 in topic.scss), and .panel (only margin-left: auto and order: 3) never set min-width: 0, overflow: hidden, or flex-shrink: 0. Flex items default to min-width: auto, so they will not shrink below their content minimum, and margin-left: auto only eats positive free space — it does not stop overflow. A wide site logo (this file only sets #site-logo max-height: 40px, not a max-width) or a long docked topic title plus the 32px header icons therefore overflows the bar instead of ellipsizing or wrapping. On a narrow viewport the fixed header widens the page and login/notification controls are pushed out of view. The old float: left / float: right layout kept the panel shrink-to-fit on the right and let the middle content wrap inside the header width. Give the middle item flex: 1, min-width: 0, and overflow: hidden, and set flex-shrink: 0 on .title and .panel.

false_negatives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is never invoked

ActiveModel::Serializer only calls include_<attr>? (every other hook in this file uses that name). include_website_name has no question mark, so it is dead code and the attribute is always serialized. Users with a blank or unparsable website still get website_name: null in /users/:username.json, and any condition placed in this method will not run.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same primary bug: include_website_name lacks the required '?' suffix, so the serializer does not invoke it for conditional attribute inclusion. It does not mention the golden comment's additional string-literal mutation concern, but directly matches the conditional inclusion issue.

false_positives.candidate:
website_name bypasses TL0 website hiding

website is listed in untrusted_attributes, so anonymous viewers of a trust-level 0 user do not receive user_profile.website (anti-spam: the profile must not expose a new user's site). website_name is a new public attribute and is not in that list, and its method reads object.user_profile.website directly. Anonymous clients therefore still get the host, and the path whenever the domain heuristic matches, and user.hbs renders that as the globe label. The new specs never serialize a TL0 user with Guardian.new and assert website_name is absent, so this regression is untested.

Same-domain path display is case-sensitive

website_host is taken from URI#host, which keeps the URL's casing, and is compared to Discourse.current_hostname with == and String#ends_with? (both case-sensitive). A site on example.com and a website of http://Example.com/user, or a site on forums.example.com and a website of http://Example.com/user, fails every branch and the profile shows only the host. The feature then does not show the path for ordinary mixed-case links. The specs only stub lowercase hosts.

Domain check mis-classifies hosts and misses www vs apex

The equal-label branch treats any two hosts with the same label count above 2 as the same site when every label but the first matches. On a forum at mysite.github.io or forum.co.uk, http://evil.github.io/phish and http://other.co.uk/phish are therefore rendered with the full path, not just the host. The else branch (discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host)) is true for any dotted suffix, so a website host of com or co.uk is treated as the parent of a normal forum hostname. The check is also asymmetric for the common www case: instance example.com vs website www.example.com/user does not match (label counts differ, and example.com does not end with .www.example.com), so the path is hidden, while instance www.example.com vs website example.com/user does show the path. None of these cases are covered by the new specs.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Resize listener accepts any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl

The check is `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, i.e. accept when the sender origin is any substring of discourseUrl, not when it equals the forum origin. A shorter origin that is a prefix matches: if discourseUrl is `https://discuss.example.com`, a window at `https://discuss.example.co` has index 0 and is accepted. That page can postMessage a `discourse-resize` and set the iframe height arbitrarily (hide comments or stretch the frame over the host page). Compare parsed origins for equality, and require index 0 only if a prefix check is kept.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify insufficient origin validation using indexOf, allowing an attacker-controlled origin to pass a substring check instead of requiring exact origin equality. The differing bypass examples do not change the underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage targetOrigin is the full referer, so resize is dropped

The embed layout calls `parent.postMessage(..., request.referer)`. postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`), not a full URL with path and query. Browsers drop the message (or throw) when it does not match the parent origin. embed.js also sets the iframe to `scrolling=no` and only grows it on `discourse-resize`, so the comments frame stays at the default height and clips the discussion. Pass the referer origin only (and escape it for the JS string).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: using the full referrer URL as postMessage's targetOrigin instead of scheme, host, and port, causing resize messages to fail and preventing iframe resizing.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
raw_html cook path stores and serves unsanitized HTML

Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, skipping PrettyText and Discourse's sanitizer. TopicEmbed.import persists RSS/Readability HTML with that cook method, and the embed view prints it with `raw post.cooked` (the main topic UI also treats cooked as HTML). PollFeed does `CGI.unescapeHTML` on feed content first, so entity-encoded markup becomes live tags, and Readability's allow-list still permits `javascript:`/`data:` href and src. Any feed item or fetched page can therefore plant stored XSS that runs for every forum visitor, not just inside the embed iframe. The imported-from footer makes this worse by interpolating the URL into an href with no escaping (`<a href='#{url}'>` in TopicEmbed.import), so a quote in an otherwise allowed http(s) URL breaks out of the attribute.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies the XSS caused by unescaped URL interpolation in TopicEmbed.import's generated anchor, matching the golden comment's security issue. It does not mention the nil contents NoMethodError, but it identifies the same underlying URL-escaping bug.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embed template has invalid ERB (`end if`)

`<%- end if %>` compiles to the Ruby statement `end if`, which is a SyntaxError. Rendering `/embed/best` when a topic already exists (the success path in EmbedController#best) will raise while compiling the template, so the iframe never shows highlights. It must be `<% end %>`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the invalid ERB closing statement `end if`, explain that it causes a Ruby syntax error during rendering, and recommend replacing it with `end`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed poll crashes unless every item has string content

`i.content.scrub` assumes every SimpleRSS item has a String `content`. RSS 2.0 items typically expose `description` and leave `content` nil; Atom can also omit it. Nil (or a non-string) raises NoMethodError, and because there is no rescue the hourly job aborts before later items are imported. `String#scrub` is also Ruby 2.1+ only, so this line fails on Ruby 2.0 even when content is present. Use description/content fallback and guard nil before unescaping.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: calling i.content.scrub when content is nil can crash feed processing, and it recommends falling back to description. Its additional concerns do not negate this match.

false_positives.candidate:
Unauthenticated embed URL fetch is an SSRF and topic-spam vector

import_remote uses `open(url).read` (open-uri) with no timeout, size limit, or redirect restriction. EmbedController#best is a public GET whose only gate is `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Referer is client-controlled, so any caller can spoof it and pass `embed_url` on the configured host. TopicRetriever then fetches that URL; open-uri follows redirects to arbitrary hosts (including link-local and cloud metadata). Each miss also enqueues RetrieveTopic with no controller-side dedupe, so unique URLs create unbounded jobs and, on success, topics posted as embed_by_username. open-uri is not even required from this file, so the fetch only works if some other file has already patched Kernel#open.

Embed controller spec expects a sync retrieve the action does not do

The 'no previous embed' example expects `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` during `get :best`. EmbedController#best only calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, so mocha fails this example and the job/throttle path is untested. The other success example renders `embed/best`, which currently raises SyntaxError on `end if`, so the `response.should be_success` after-hook fails as well. The spec will not pass as written and does not lock in the async behavior.

Disqus import drops category, original date, and offline permalinks

The importer no longer accepts `--category` and no longer passes `created_at` or `category` into topic creation. It now depends on `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which HTTP-fetches `t[:link]` and returns nil on any network/HTTP error. The following comment import is skipped entirely when that fetch fails, so a dead or blocked article URL drops the whole Disqus thread instead of creating the previous permalink stub. Category placement and original thread timestamps are also lost, and a single failed fetch aborts the rest of the file because nothing rescues `open`.

embed_url is varchar(255) but used as the unique lookup key

`t.string :embed_url` is a 255-character varchar, with a unique index on that column. TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed and import look up the full URL. Article and RSS links with tracking query strings routinely exceed 255 characters, so insert raises and the topic is never associated; truncated values would also collide or miss on lookup. Store embed_url as text (and index a hash if a unique constraint is still required).

content_sha1 is advanced even when the post is not updated

On change, import always calls `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` after `revise!`, without checking that revise!/save succeeded. PostRevisor#revise! returns false when raw is unchanged and still returns true if `save` fails; either way the SHA is overwritten. The next poll then treats the feed item as already imported and never retries, so the topic body stays stale. If the linked post was deleted, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(post)` raises, which aborts the rest of the feed run. Update the SHA only after a successful save, and skip or recreate when the post is gone.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition overwrites the width/height API

Ruby does not overload by arity, so downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) on line 149 replaces downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) on line 145. The width/height wrapper never exists at runtime. Callers that still use the previous signature — numeric max width and max height, which this pull request does not update anywhere else — now bind the height integer to opts. optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] and raises NoMethodError instead of building a widthxheight geometry, so those calls 500.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify duplicate downsize definitions where the dimensions-string version overrides the separate width/height version, breaking callers using the original API. The candidate adds runtime failure details but describes the same underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client size check hardcoded to 10MB for every type

validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments each honored their admin setting. It now always uses 10 * 1024. Attachments larger than 10MB are rejected even when max_attachment_size_kb allows them, and attachments between the real attachment limit and 10MB pass the client and fail only on the server. Images are capped at 10MB regardless of max_image_size_kb, so a site that allows larger images cannot upload them from the browser. The 413 handler on line 246 uses the same hardcode, so the dialog always claims the limit is 10240 KB even when the web server or site setting differs.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same hardcoded 10MB limit ignoring per-type Discourse site settings, causing client/server limit divergence, and also notes the same hardcode in the 413 handler.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
80% geometry breaks animation and does not enforce the size limit

The new call passes "80%" and allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails. When that setting is false, downsize_instructions runs convert with a [0] frame selector, so a large animated GIF or multi-page image is permanently flattened to the first frame in the stored original; that setting is about thumbnails, not the upload. When it is true, gifsicle --resize-fit is given "80%", but it requires a pixel size such as 100x100, so it exits non-zero. The failure is ignored, and after five attempts the still-oversized file is passed to Upload.create_for anyway. The loop also does not fail the upload if the file is still larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb after five 80% passes, so the comment's "reduced to allowed size" guarantee is not enforced for JPEGs or PNGs either.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies the same bug: with allow_animated_thumbnails enabled, passing "80%" to gifsicle --resize-fit fails because it requires WxH pixel geometry, and the ignored failure leaves the image oversized. Its additional concerns do not negate this match.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsize reads and writes the same tempfile

OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both source and destination. convert (and gifsicle when animation is enabled) opens the output for writing before the input is fully read, and ImageMagick truncates that path immediately. This tempfile is the only copy of the upload, so a large image can become empty or partial before Upload.create_for. The loop also ignores downsize's false return, so a failed conversion is retried against the already truncated file and then handed to create_for. Write to a separate tempfile and replace the original only after a successful non-empty result.

API URL downloads capped at a hardcoded 10MB for all types

FileHelper.download's limit changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to 10.megabytes for every upload type, not only images that will be downsized. Non-image API URL uploads are therefore cut off at 10MB even when max_attachment_size_kb is higher, and they are no longer tied to the attachment setting at all. Image URL uploads also cannot exceed 10MB when max_image_size_kb is configured above that, so the admin setting and the new downscale path disagree.

No input size ceiling before repeated ImageMagick runs

The browser and the URL-download path are capped at 10MB, but the multipart file branch never checks an upper bound before the downsize loop. The client check is bypassable: any logged-in user can POST a huge image and force up to five ImageMagick convert runs plus ImageOptim inside Scheduler::Defer. A decompression bomb or a multi-hundred-megabyte image is fully decoded on each attempt, which is a CPU and memory exhaustion path. Reject or cap the input before calling downsize, and stop if an attempt does not shrink the file.

No tests for downsizing or the new size caps

This change alters client limits, URL download limits, and runs a five-iteration ImageMagick downsize before Upload.create_for, but no tests were added. Failures such as in-place conversion, the overwritten downsize signature, attachment versus image limits, a file that stays over max_image_size_kb, and animated GIF handling would not be caught before merge.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing TopicUser crashes unsubscribe and the change is not recorded

TopicUser.find_by can return nil (user never had a topic_users row, or it was removed). The next line calls tu.notification_level and raises NoMethodError, so the unsubscribe link 500s instead of muting the topic. When a row does exist, tu.save! writes notification_level directly and skips TopicUser.change, so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at stay unset and no MessageBus notification_level_change is published. update_last_read auto-promotes to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and view time exceeds the auto-track threshold, which silently undoes the unsubscribe on a later visit. Other open tabs also keep the old level.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies the same nil-pointer issue: TopicUser.find_by may return nil, and calling tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError. Its additional concerns do not negate this direct match.

false_positives.candidate:
Unsubscribe GET is not idempotent and does not stop topic emails

GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe changes notification_level on every request: tracking/watching (above regular) is set to regular, and regular or muted is set to muted. A watching user — the usual case for topic notification mail, including category auto-watch — is only dropped to regular, so reply, mention, quote, and category-watch emails continue, despite the email and page copy saying notifications for that topic will stop. Because the same transition runs again on refresh, prefetch, or a second click, that user is then muted. The action is also not safe to retry: there is no confirmation step and no check that the level was already updated.

Topic unsubscribe is a cookie-authenticated GET with no recipient token

Both unsubscribe routes are GET and TopicsController#unsubscribe mutates notification state with no CSRF token and no per-recipient key (unlike digest unsubscribe). Rails does not check authenticity tokens on GET, so a logged-in user's browser will apply the change for any third-party page that can trigger the URL (img, redirect, or link prefetch). The link is also not bound to the email recipient: whoever is logged in is the account that is changed, and a logged-out recipient is not unsubscribed until after a login round-trip.

Unsubscribe template will not resolve for the new route

The route is registered as a top-level topicUnsubscribe (/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe), and the route, controller, and view files are all named topic-unsubscribe, so Ember looks up the template topic-unsubscribe. This file is registered as topic/unsubscribe (the nested topic.unsubscribe name). Nothing sets templateName or renderTemplate, so the confirmation copy and the topic-notifications-button never render. After the Rails action mutates notification level, the user gets a missing-template error instead of the unsubscribe page. The Ember route also never calls an unsubscribe API itself, so a client-side transition to this URL would show the "you will stop receiving notifications" text without changing the level even if the template name were fixed.

No tests for per-topic unsubscribe behavior

The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into Email::MessageBuilder so the new %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation does not raise. Nothing asserts that the topic link is actually rendered, and there is no request/controller coverage for unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching vs regular vs muted transitions, a second request not changing the level again, slug redirect, or the login/CSRF constraints. The level rules are easy to get wrong and would regress silently.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Empty updateMany throws after every cache write

fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) after upserting CalendarCache. Prisma Client rejects updateMany when data is an empty object ("Argument data needs at least one argument"), so this throws on every successful cache fill, including Google webhook refreshes and the refill at the end of unwatchCalendar. Callers that treat the throw as a sync/watch failure will retry, record errors, and can eventually stop watching the calendar even though the cache write already succeeded. An empty payload also does not reliably bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. The new repository method types data as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which is not assignable to updateMany's UpdateManyMutationInput. Pass an explicit update such as { updatedAt: new Date() }.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same empty-data updateManyByCredentialId call, explicitly notes that it fails to bump updatedAt, and recommends setting updatedAt explicitly. Its additional claims about exceptions and input types do not negate the match to the golden issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook helper fails on Linux and writes the wrong env file

The script updates GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with sed -i '', which is BSD/macOS sed and fails on GNU sed, so the env update does not work on Linux. ENV_FILE is ../.env relative to the current working directory, not the script or repo root. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore targets a path outside the repo, and if that file is missing touch creates it and writes the tunnel URL there instead of the project .env. Resolve the env path from the script directory and use a portable in-place edit.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies the same issue: sed -i '' uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails with GNU sed on Linux. The additional env-path concern does not negate the match.

true_positives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Deleting cache does not stop watches that recreate it

deleteCacheHandler only runs calendarCache.deleteMany for the credential. It does not clear Google channel fields or stop notification channels. Webhook handling calls fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache, which writes CalendarCache again, so for any watched Google calendar the rows return on the next push and the delete looks like it failed. The new confirm_delete_cache string says the action cannot be undone, which is false while watches are active. Either stop watches the way unwatchCalendar does before deleting, or tell the user the cache will be rebuilt and trigger a refetch. The access check also throws a plain Error, which tRPC reports as an internal 500 instead of NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN.
true_positives.reasoning: Although the candidate primarily discusses cache recreation, it explicitly identifies the same authentication/access-check issue: throwing a plain Error causes tRPC to return an internal 500 rather than an appropriate structured error such as FORBIDDEN.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache timestamp format is a type error and ignores locale

The last-updated label always does new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }).format(new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)). cacheUpdatedAt is Date | null | undefined, and hasCache is a separate boolean, so TypeScript does not narrow it; new Date(cacheUpdatedAt) is not assignable under strictNullChecks and should fail typecheck. The formatter is also hardcoded to en-US, so the translated cache_last_updated string still shows a US timestamp for every locale. Format only a narrowed Date with the active locale.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies the hardcoded en-US date formatter and recommends using the active locale, matching the golden issue. Its additional type-checking concern does not negate this match.

false_positives.candidate:
Cache delete does not refresh connected calendars

deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (or apps.integrations). The calendar settings query lives in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper and onChanged is often omitted, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows the previous Last updated time and the delete action. Users are told the cache was deleted while the UI keeps offering to delete it until a full reload.

Cache status counts expired rows as live cache

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups every CalendarCache row for the credential and takes max(updatedAt), with no expiresAt >= now filter. Availability reads ignore expired rows, but the settings dropdown treats any truthy cacheUpdatedAt as live cache and offers Delete cached data. Credentials whose cache has fully expired still show a last-updated time. Restrict the query to unexpired rows, and return no status when every row is expired.

Existing cache rows are stamped with migration time

updatedAt is added as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so every existing CalendarCache row gets the migration execution time rather than the last free/busy write. The new status query uses max(updatedAt), so after deploy every Google credential that already has cache will show that deploy timestamp as Last updated until the next Prisma upsert. Backfill from a closer signal (for example expiresAt minus the cache TTL) or keep legacy updatedAt null and only display a timestamp after a real update.

No tests for cache delete authorization or status

deleteCache is a new mutation that deletes CalendarCache rows after an ownership check, and getCacheStatusByCredentialIds changes what connectedCalendars returns, but there are no unit or integration tests. A dropped userId filter, deleting another user's credential, or stale cacheUpdatedAt after delete would not be caught. Cover owner success, rejection of another user's credentialId, and that connected calendars no longer report cache after deletion.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours recheck rejects valid slots whenever a host has more than one window

checkIfIsAvailable now runs for every isFixed host, and personal events, collective events, and round-robin fixed hosts are all marked isFixed. The new working-hours test uses Array.find and returns unavailable if the slot falls outside any single window whose days include the slot's UTC weekday. A host with a lunch break, or a single local range that getWorkingHours splits across UTC midnight into two entries on the same day, therefore fails the check for every slot: a 10:00 slot inside 09:00–12:00 is still outside 13:00–17:00, so find matches and the slot is dropped. The booking page then shows no times. The condition is also inverted for days off: if no window lists that weekday, find matches nothing and the host is treated as free, so a fixed host who does not work that day is not actually blocked. The end minute is copied from slot start (hour*60+minute of slotStartTime, not slot end), so a slot that starts inside a window but whose event length runs past endTime is accepted. Net effect is both false unavailability for ordinary split schedules and false availability outside hours.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies that the end minute is calculated from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, allowing slots that extend past working hours. This matches the golden issue, despite also describing other bugs.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Date-override hit skips busy times and mishandles multiple or empty overrides

On a day that has a date override, if the slot is considered inside an override, checkIfIsAvailable sets dateOverrideExist and returns true immediately, before the busy/booking loop. A fixed host (including every personal or collective host) who blocked 15:00 with a calendar event or Cal booking, but has a date override covering that time, is reported free, so the slot stays bookable and can double-book. The same find() treats "outside this one override" as a hard unavailable: two override windows on the same day reject a slot that sits in only one of them, because the other window's callback returns true. Zero-length overrides (the unavailable-day convention, start equal to end) are detected with dayjs object ===, which is never true for two instances, so that branch never runs. With the new CLI default --flusher-processes 1, one process owns every assigned partition, so this is the default path whenever a consumer has more than one partition. The value is also unique per partition assignment, so rebalances create a high-cardinality series. wait_produce uses the key shards while produce uses shard, so the two timers cannot be correlated. true_positives.golden_comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

If that consumes the budget, remaining_time <= 0 and the loop breaks without process.terminate() for every flusher process. close() intentionally does not stop these processes (to avoid a Redis memory spike at the start of rebalance), so join is the only force-stop path. Arroyo calls join with a finite timeout on shutdown and rebalance, and the consumer process stays alive across rebalance, so an un-killed flusher keeps flushing shards this consumer no longer owns. Those segments race the new assignee and are produced again to the buffered-segments topic. The wait is also sequential, so one slow process can exhaust the deadline and skip terminate() for the rest. The previous single-process join always terminated after the wait. Every access-token issuance path needs to set the real grant, or initToken must fail instead of writing na for a request whose grant is known.

When the prefix before ':' is not 6 characters, the exception says Incorrect token id: '<full id>'. Expected length of 6. The full jti is a 6-character prefix plus ':' plus a UUID, so the message describes the wrong length and will send operators looking at the wrong field when decode starts failing requests.

If that stream is empty (storage accepted updateCredential but does not implement getCredentials), if the model has no secretData, or if every code is already used, rendering the recovery-code page throws NoSuchElementException or a JSON error instead of a challenge. updateCredential saves input.getChallengeResponse() verbatim in credentialData, which is the JSON array of raw codes, not hashes. isValid then returns true if any stored code equals the input and does not remove the match or require it to be the next unused code. getCredentials ignores that stored model and calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues on the original list, which assigns a new id and marks every code unused. So the code index shown at login never advances, allCodesUsed() is never true, removeStoredCredentialById cannot target the real id, and a captured code can be replayed indefinitely. testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only signs in once with code 0, so it does not catch replay, a stuck index, plaintext persistence, or failure to force regeneration.

That is the same id issue the golden comment raises, though the candidate bundles it with other concerns.

It drops generatedAt, the user label, and the hashed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel that createFromValues already built. RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean and RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator then take the first federated credential of this type and pass it to RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel, which requires secretData in Keycloak's hashed schema. A provider that stores the updateCredential value and returns that CredentialModel (secretData null, credentialData = the raw JSON) — the same shape this PR's test storage saves, and the same pattern used for OTP — makes the login form throw while parsing, or throws after isValid already accepted the code, so recovery-code login never completes. After credentialManager().isValid succeeds, this authenticator assumes the credential row was already updated and, when allCodesUsed() is true, deletes it with removeStoredCredentialById. That side effect exists only in the local recovery-code credential provider. For the new user-storage path, isValid is delegated to the storage provider and this method never writes the remaining codes back with updateCredential. removeStoredCredentialById only deletes credentials stored in Keycloak's database, not credentials owned by user storage, and the id on a federated model is not a local credential id. @EnableFeature(RECOVERY_CODES, skipRestart = true) only flips the runtime profile flag. This PR does not change any operator production code that runs the check, and UpdateCommandDistTest never asserts an exit code: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks stderr text, and testWrongVersions only checks the incompatibility message. A caller still treating 4 as "incompatible, shut the cluster down first" will now take that path when the preview feature is merely off, and will not treat a real incompatibility (now exit 3) as recreate. That is the decision this tool exists to make; getting it backwards is either an unnecessary outage or a rolling update across incompatible versions. The implementation does not evaluate compatibility in this case: UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata print "Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled." and return FEATURE_DISABLED before any metadata is read. The guide tells automation to rely on these codes. Describing 4 as a negative compatibility result will cause pipelines to recreate or drain the cluster when the only required action is to enable the feature and rerun the check.

createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, so spec.features.enabled is left unset for the null cases of testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount. Those cases still call deployKeycloak(..., true), which waits until the CR is ready, and then assert an upgrade status. The operator guide added in this PR says that while the feature is preview it must be enabled or the Operator will fail, including for the default <not set> strategy that mimics 26.1. As written, the default-strategy tests do not meet that precondition and will time out if the warning is true. If they pass, the warning is false and tells every operator user to turn on a preview feature or expect a failed reconcile. Enable the feature for every parameter value, and append it to any features already on the CR instead of setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...)) replacing the whole list, or narrow the caution if the default path is intentionally exempt.

Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. true_positives.golden_comment: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

The schema's all-clients resource is named "Clients" (init sets both name and type to the resource type). A user who only has a type-level grant therefore gets a set containing the literal "Clients" rather than every client id, and callers that filter with client.getId() match nothing. Object resources are only included if their type was set to Clients; getOrCreateResource creates them by name and scopes and never calls setType, so per-client grants are also omitted if no other layer sets the type. Listing and role-mapping UIs that rely on this set will hide clients the user is allowed to access. The type resource should be expanded or skipped, and returned ids must be real client ids.

Per-client resources have no type set and are therefore missed. As a result, callers expecting real client ids will fail to match.

true_positives.golden_comment: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.

When no per-client resource exists, hasPermission assigns getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately calls PolicyStore.findByResource(server, resource) with no null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null if the "Clients" resource was never created. findByResource dereferences that resource and throws NullPointerException, so canView/canManage/canConfigure/canMapRoles return 500 instead of false. AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already non-null and never adds the new Clients resource type or the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite). Any realm that enabled admin permissions before this schema change keeps the old resource server, so the first per-client check 500s and creating a Clients permission fails because those scopes are absent. init needs an upgrade path, and the evaluator must treat a missing type resource as deny.

It also says a null check is needed and that a missing resource should be treated as deny. The extra point about upgrading init is additional context and does not change the core match.

true_positives.golden_comment: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
true_positives.matched_candidate:
V2 throws on token exchange and permissions API

MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now always returns ClientPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, but canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, and getPermissions all throw UnsupportedOperationException. Token exchange calls AdminPermissions.management().clients().canExchangeTo and will fail the request with a server error for every realm that has the feature enabled, even if token-exchange permissions are unused. The admin client management-permissions endpoint calls isPermissionsEnabled, then resource and getPermissions, so opening fine-grained permissions for a client 500s. These methods are still part of the live ClientPermissions contract; they need a V2 behavior (or a safe deny/empty result), not an exception. getEvaluationContext is unused dead code left from an unfinished exchange check.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate's main focus is the UnsupportedOperationException problem. Its last sentence, though, explicitly says getEvaluationContext is unused dead code, which is the same issue the golden comment raises.

false_positives.candidate:
Role-mapping checks ignore manage-clients admins

canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission and never treat AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS as sufficient. This class fully replaces ClientPermissions whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and V1 granted those operations to holders of manage-clients (including master-realm and realm admins) before any fine-grained policy was consulted. canManage and canManageClientScopes still short-circuit on that role, so the same admin can update a client but is denied mapping client roles, composite roles, and client-scope roles. Admin console role-mapping calls fail with 403 even when no FGAP policy was meant to restrict that admin. The new tests only cover a user without manage-clients, so they do not catch this.

Per-client resource hides all-clients allow and deny

hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) loads the object resource by client id and, if that row exists, evaluates only that resource. The all-clients resource is consulted only when no object resource exists. Creating any object permission (for example VIEW on one client) therefore drops realm-wide grants such as MANAGE/CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES on "Clients" for that client, so an admin who can manage every client loses manage on any client that also has an object-level permission. The same short-circuit skips a realm-wide negative permission, so a deny-all policy on Clients does not apply to a client that already has an object resource and a positive object permission. Authorization becomes order-dependent and can both lock out legitimate admins and bypass a type-level deny.

Client permission resources have no display name

getResourceName only resolves Users resources to a username. Client object resources are stored under the client UUID (resolveClient returns client.getId()) and getOrCreateResource never sets a display name, so the fallback resource.getDisplayName() is null. Admin APIs that label permission resources will show a blank name for every client permission, and a deleted client is not reported as missing the way a missing user is (ModelIllegalStateException). This method needs a Clients branch that loads the client and returns its clientId, and a defined error if the client is gone.

requireView javadoc describes a boolean result

requireView is void and throws ForbiddenException, but its new javadoc says it returns true if canView() returns true. requireViewClientScopes (line 101) has the same error: it says it returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true. Callers reading the interface will treat these as predicates instead of enforcing methods. The comments should match requireManage/requireList and state that they throw when the corresponding can* check is false.

true_positives.golden_comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)

getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider

The CryptoProvider contract says getBouncyCastleProvider returns the non-FIPS or FIPS BouncyCastle provider. This implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is the platform provider for the default keystore type (typically SUN), not BC or BCFIPS. Callers use that Provider's name and instance for Cipher/Signature/CertificateFactory and for BouncyIntegration. Algorithms that exist only under BC (AES/CBC/PKCS7Padding, many JOSE/JWE transforms, BCFKS) will fail or silently run outside FIPS when this provider is the one CryptoIntegration selected. Elytron returns null rather than a lookalike; this should not hand back an unrelated JCA provider.
true_positives.reasoning: Both say getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default keystore provider instead of the BouncyCastle provider. This is the same issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
true_positives.matched_candidate:
New abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations

order() was added as an abstract interface method with no default. CryptoProvider is a public SPI in keycloak-common. Existing downstream or custom implementations (and any already-compiled class) will not have this method. ServiceLoader instantiates every provider and then calls order() during sort, so one old implementation on the classpath throws AbstractMethodError and aborts detection entirely, even if a newer provider is also present. That turns a compatible server startup into a hard failure. A default method (for example returning 0) would keep old providers loadable and still let the new order-200 providers win.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same problem: adding an abstract order() method to the CryptoProvider interface breaks existing implementations, which hurts backward compatibility. The candidate goes further and suggests a default method as the fix, but the underlying issue is identical.

false_positives.candidate:
Equal-order crypto providers are now chosen silently

detectProvider used to fail fast when ServiceLoader found more than one CryptoProvider. It now sorts by order() and keeps the first, only logging the rest. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so a classpath that contains both FIPS and non-FIPS (or Elytron and default) no longer errors. ServiceLoader order is classpath order, and sorted() is stable, so which full provider wins is environment-dependent. ServiceLoader also instantiates every provider before the sort, so FIPS1402Provider still inserts BCFIPS/BCJSSE and rewrites key/trust manager security properties even if the non-FIPS provider is the one selected (and DefaultCryptoProvider still registers BouncyCastle). A FIPS deployment can therefore keep running in a mixed or non-FIPS mode instead of refusing to start. Tie at the winning order should still be a hard error, and FIPS must outrank the non-FIPS providers if silent preference is intended.

AuthzClient.create can permanently install the stub crypto provider

AuthzClient.create now calls CryptoIntegration.init with AuthzClient's own classloader, and init only selects a provider when the static cryptoProvider field is still null. That selection is process-wide and never refreshed. AuthzClientCryptoProvider is registered via META-INF/services and implements almost every CryptoProvider method by throwing UnsupportedOperationException, with order 100. If create() runs before the server calls init with a classloader that can see DefaultCryptoProvider or FIPS1402Provider (deployment/module classloader that only exposes the authz-client service file, embedded startup, or a test that builds an AuthzClient first), the stub is locked in for the JVM. Later server init is a no-op, so token signing, PEM handling, and the other crypto entry points fail or use the incomplete provider even though a real one is on the server classpath.

ECDSA test does not compile in this module

ECDSAAlgorithmTest imports org.keycloak.crypto.ECDSAAlgorithm and org.keycloak.crypto.JavaAlgorithm. Those types live in the server SPI (the crypto modules already import them from there), not in keycloak-core. authz/client/pom.xml only adds junit and hamcrest; its compile/test classpath is still just keycloak-core plus HTTP/Jackson. server-spi is not a dependency, and keycloak-core cannot depend on server-spi without a cycle. testCompile of keycloak-authz-client-tests therefore fails with a missing org.keycloak.crypto package, so the new coverage never runs.

ECDSA transcoding test never checks a real signature

The only assertion is that asn1derToConcatenatedRS and concatenatedRSToASN1DER round-trip each other. The key pair is generated once with KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC"), which is P-256 on standard JDKs, and that same key is used for ES256, ES384, and ES512. ES384/ES512 signature lengths are 96 and 132 bytes and their DER SEQUENCEs need long-form lengths once R and S match P-384/P-521, but a P-256 signature stays short and is only zero-padded to those lengths. Nothing calls Signature.verify on the original DER or on the re-encoded DER, and there is no known-answer vector. A self-consistent but non-interoperable encoder (wrong tag, non-minimal INTEGER, broken long-form length) still passes, which is the failure mode this provider exists to prevent.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.

true_positives.golden_comment: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative cursor offsets raise ValueError, they do not paginate

When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a negative start (paginator.py:880-882). The audit-log endpoint always passes enable_advanced_features=True. Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ does not support negative indexes and raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported"); it does not compile SQL or clamp the range. Cursor.from_string accepts a negative offset (for example "0:-5:0"), and that value is client-controlled, so an optimized_pagination request with such a cursor returns HTTP 500. The fallback branch (paginator.py:884-886) does the same for previous-page cursors. The comments that this reaches rows past normal pagination bounds, and that queryset permissions make that safe, are false: the call fails before a query runs. Negative offsets should be rejected with BadPaginationError, not sliced.

The candidate names ValueError where the golden says AssertionError, but that difference depends on the Django version and the underlying issue is identical.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Optimized paginator crashes on datetime audit-log keys

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (paginator.py:840) runs math.floor/math.ceil on the order-by attribute, and value_from_cursor (paginator.py:843) returns the raw cursor integer. OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint wires this class in with order_by="-datetime" (organization_auditlogs.py:79-80). AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so any optimized_pagination request that returns at least one row raises TypeError inside build_cursor when it calls get_item_key, and the client gets a 500. A later request that supplies a numeric cursor also fails in build_queryset, which compares the timestamp column to an integer instead of converting the cursor the way DateTimePaginator does (milliseconds to a timezone-aware datetime). The new path is unusable for real audit logs; it needs DateTimePaginator's key conversion, not Paginator's numeric key logic.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same issue as the golden comment: get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on the datetime order_by key in the audit logs endpoint, which raises a TypeError.

false_positives.candidate:
BasePaginator silently rewrites negative forward offsets for every list API

The new start_offset logic is in BasePaginator.get_result, which Paginator and DateTimePaginator share, so it changes cursor pagination for every endpoint, not just audit logs. For a non-previous cursor, a negative offset is rewritten to 0 and the first page is returned. Previously queryset[negative:stop] raised ValueError. Cursors are not clamped in Cursor.from_string, so a client can send "0:-1:0". build_cursor still derives the next offset from the original negative cursor.offset (offset + limit when the sort key is unchanged), so Link headers can keep publishing a negative offset and a client can loop on the same first page. Previous-page cursors still pass the negative offset through and 500. This is not a performance fix and should be reverted or turned into an explicit BadPaginationError.

No tests for the new paginator or the shared offset change

The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, switches OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint to it when optimized_pagination=true, and changes slicing in BasePaginator.get_result, but no tests were added or updated. A request against the audit-log endpoint with optimized_pagination=true and at least one AuditLogEntry would have failed on the datetime TypeError; a cursor with a negative offset would have failed on Django's ValueError; and existing paginator tests do not lock the new BasePaginator behavior for negative forward offsets. true_positives.golden_comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
BuildIndex no longer single-flights per key

BuildIndex used to hold cacheMu for the whole build, which also blocked GetIndex and serialized builders. The lock is now taken only to publish b.cache[key]. getOrCreateIndex is still check-then-act (GetIndex, and on nil call build/BuildIndex) and has no per-key lock or singleflight. Concurrent first searches, watch events, or init workers for the same NamespacedResource therefore build two bleve indexes. The later cache write blindly overwrites the earlier one, so one caller keeps writing and searching an index that is no longer in the cache while everyone else uses the other. The discarded index is never closed (memory and file-handle leak). For file indexes both builders use the same directory, so the second bleve.New fails and that caller gets an error even if the first build succeeded.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same race: the cacheMu lock was narrowed to cover only the cache assignment, so concurrent builders can build the same index for one key. The candidate states this directly and adds consequences.

false_positives.candidate:
File indexes cannot be reopened, so eager init crash-loops

When size exceeds FileThreshold, BuildIndex always calls bleve.New on a stable path (Root/namespace/resource.group) and never bleve.Open. bleve.New fails if that directory already exists. A successful build, a killed process, or a failed init that already created the directory leaves the path on disk. Init now runs inside NewResourceServer and any BuildIndex error aborts server construction, so the next start hits the same bleve.New error and the process cannot boot until the directory is deleted by hand. The removed log was the only hint that an existing index/RV should be reused; the TODO remains unimplemented.

Index init workers race on shared err

searchSupport.init starts initWorkers goroutines that all do `_, _, err = s.build(...)` and `return err`, plus `totalBatchesIndexed++`, on variables owned by the outer function with no mutex or atomic. That is a data race. One worker can return another worker's nil and hide a failed namespace build, so startup continues after an index failed (the opposite of the comment that any init failure must block startup), or a success can be overwritten and fail startup incorrectly. The span attribute namespaced_indexed is also racy. This function is now on the blocking startup path.

Postgres storage-server startup test is skipped

TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer is the integration coverage for the storage-server target coming up and serving /metrics. This change makes NewResourceServer run unified-storage Init (stats, index build, watch) during that startup, which this test previously never reached because it never issued a storage RPC. The PR skips the test on postgres with a TODO that it fails in Drone, so the CI job that would catch a postgres-specific eager-init failure no longer runs it.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

false_positives.candidate:

try_incident_threshold treats failure_issue_threshold as a lookback window, then opens an incident whenever none of those rows are CheckInStatus.OK. true_positives.golden_comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.

Dataclass defaults are evaluated once when the class body is executed, not on each construction, and datetime is not a default_factory. Every AssignmentSource created via from_integration or from_dict without an explicit queued value therefore shares the single timestamp captured when the module was imported. The field is meant to record when that assignment change was queued and is copied into every outbound task payload via to_dict, but rapid successive assignee updates (the case this PR is fixing) are indistinguishable by time, and freeze_time in tests cannot affect it. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each source gets its own timestamp.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same bug. The default `queued = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class definition or import time, so every instance shares the same timestamp. The candidate also suggests the matching fix, `default_factory`.

true_positives.golden_comment: to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.

to_dict() is dataclasses.asdict, so the dict passed to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async in sync_group_assignee_outbound includes queued as a raw datetime. That task previously accepted only ints, a bool, and None. A datetime is not JSON-serializable: under a JSON task serializer, apply_async raises TypeError while handling the inbound webhook, after GroupAssignee.assign/deassign has already written the assignee. The webhook then errors, linked integrations other than the source never get the update, and retries repeat the failure. from_dict is also not an inverse of to_dict: it splats the dict into the constructor and only catches TypeError/ValueError, so an ISO-string queued value is accepted as a str rather than parsed, and any malformed payload returns None. The outbound task treats None as "no source" and calls should_sync without a source, which re-enables the echo and brings the sync loop back. Eager task tests never cross this serialization boundary, so they do not catch it.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same problem. to_dict() leaves queued as a raw datetime, and passing that dict through apply_async can fail JSON serialization and cause enqueue errors.

false_positives.candidate:
Cross-integration and deassign cycle behavior untested

The new test only assigns with AssignmentSource.from_integration on the same integration that owns the single linked external issue and asserts sync_assignee_outbound is not called. Nothing covers a second linked integration with a different id, which is the case the change claims must still propagate, so a regression that skips every outbound sync whenever any AssignmentSource is present would still pass. Inbound deassign now also threads assignment_source through GroupAssignee.deassign, but the deassign test still only expects assignment_source=None and never asserts that a matching source suppresses the outbound unassign. Both paths are required to stop the Jira assignee loop.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
