true_positives.golden_comment: The test test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling has a docstring that doesn't match the test implementation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Error-handling test asserts the opposite of its docstring and races the commit loop

test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling says processing errors must not block offset commits, but the assertion requires the partition to be absent from committed_offsets. The worker always complete_offset in a finally, including when the patched processor raises, so a commit of offset 102 (101+1) is the actual behavior and the assertion fails if it happens. The test only sleeps 0.2s after the calls return, while the commit thread waits 1.0s before its first commit, so the assertion usually passes only because the commit has not run yet and fails when scheduling is slower. It neither locks the intended contract nor reliably passes.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate says the error-handling test's assertion contradicts its docstring. That is the same mismatch the golden comment describes. The candidate also raises a race condition, but the core issue is the same.

false_positives.candidate:
Shared queue pool is destroyed on rebalance and later messages are committed unprocessed

FixedQueuePool is created once on ResultsStrategyFactory and reused by every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy. Strategy.close() (queue_consumer.py) calls queue_pool.shutdown(), which sets each worker's shutdown flag, calls Queue.shutdown(), and joins the workers. Arroyo closes the strategy and calls create_with_partitions again on the same factory on every partition revoke/assign, so the next strategy is handed a pool whose queues reject puts and whose workers are dead. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit then hits the bare except, logs, and add_offset+complete_offset without ever running the result processor. The commit thread treats that as success and commits offset+1. After the first rebalance or consumer restart-in-process, every uptime result is acknowledged and dropped. The same except also permanently drops any message whose grouping function or enqueue raises, instead of letting the consumer retry.

Offsets are committed from a background thread against a non-thread-safe Kafka consumer

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy starts a daemon commit thread that calls the Arroyo commit callback (and therefore the Kafka consumer's stage/commit path) every second. The consumer thread is simultaneously in poll()/submit(). confluent-kafka Consumer objects are not thread-safe, and Arroyo's commit policy mutates shared offset state that is only used from the processing thread elsewhere. Concurrent commit and poll can crash the consumer, skip commits, or publish a torn offset map. terminate() only sets shutdown_event and does not join this thread, so it can still be inside commit_function after the processor has closed the consumer. close() joins the thread for at most 5s and then continues, so a slow commit leaves two commit threads if a new strategy is created. Commit from poll() on the consumer thread instead.

Queues are unbounded, so the claimed backpressure does not exist

Each work queue is created with queue.Queue() and no maxsize, and submit() always put()s without blocking. The class docstring says queues provide natural backpressure, but poll() only emits a gauge and never pauses the consumer. A slow subscription (the case this mode is meant to isolate) makes its queue retain every subsequent message in memory while the main thread keeps fetching. Offset commits cannot advance past that item, so the process holds the entire uncommitted backlog until it OOMs. get_committable_offsets also walks range(start, max_offset+1) under the partition lock, so a large backlog stalls every worker's complete_offset for the duration of that scan.

Shutdown abandons queued work and can block for num_queues * 5s

FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True before draining, and OrderedQueueWorker.run only calls get() while that flag is false. After the current item, the worker exits even if Queue.shutdown(immediate=False) would still return queued items, so those items are never processed and never completed. close() stops and joins the commit thread before joining workers, so items that do finish during shutdown are not committed either. join() ignores its timeout and calls close(). On a deploy/rebalance, in-flight uptime results are redelivered and applied twice (duplicate incidents/occurrences). Joins are also sequential with a 5s timeout each, so 20 workers stuck in slow handlers make close()/terminate() block for about 100s and still drop the work.

An exception in the worker finally kills the only thread for that queue forever

OrderedQueueWorker has no supervisor. complete_offset and metrics.gauge run in the same finally block with no handler, and run() has no outer try around the loop. If gauge (or complete_offset) raises, the thread exits. That queue is the only worker for every group hashed to it, and nothing restarts it. Any offset already queued there stays in outstanding forever, so get_committable_offsets cannot advance that partition. The consumer keeps polling, health checks still pass because poll() only records queue depth, and commits for the partition stop until the process is restarted.

Worker threads never reset Django DB connections, so one DB error drops later results

OrderedQueueWorker calls result_processor on a long-lived thread and never calls django.db.close_old_connections(). Django only runs connection health checks and obsolete-connection cleanup on the request path, which these threads do not have. After an idle timeout, failover, or OperationalError, that thread's connection stays dead. ResultProcessor.__call__ swallows the exception, and the worker's finally still complete_offset, so the failed check is committed and will not be retried. Every later message on that same queue fails the same way and is also acknowledged. One transient DB blip silently disables 1/num_queues of subscription processing until the consumer restarts.

Uptime --mode help still describes the wrong execution model

uptime_options() now accepts thread-queue-parallel, but the help text is still "The mode to process results in. Parallel uses multithreading." The parallel mode uses a multiprocessing pool, batched-parallel uses a thread pool, and thread-queue-parallel uses one thread per queue. Operators enabling the new flag get no description of what it does or that --max-workers is the queue count rather than a thread-pool size.

Django QuerySet rejects a negative slice bound with ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported") before any SQL runs, so a cursor such as 0:-1:0 returns HTTP 500. Cursor.from_string already accepts a negative offset, so any caller who can set the query flag can trigger it. The comments claim the ORM handles negative offsets and that this reaches rows outside normal pagination bounds; it does neither, and it does not bypass the organization filter.

The candidate adds the consequence (Django raises ValueError, giving HTTP 500), but the underlying issue is identical.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Global paginator now mishandles negative cursor offsets

BasePaginator.get_result is shared by every DateTimePaginator/Paginator list endpoint. It now uses max(0, offset) for non-previous cursors and passes previous-cursor offsets through unchanged. A normal non-negative offset behaves as before, but a next cursor with a negative offset used to error and now silently starts at 0, returning the first page instead of the requested window. A previous cursor with a negative offset is still handed to the queryset, and Django raises ValueError, 500ing the request. The new comment says the queryset handles negative offsets; it does not. This change is unrelated to span buffering.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly says that previous-cursor negative offsets are passed unchanged to the queryset, which causes a Django ValueError. That is the same issue as the golden comment: no clamping when is_prev is True, so negative offsets reach queryset slicing.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.

Optimized audit-log paginator crashes on datetime ordering

With optimized_pagination=true and a superuser or global-access member, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint switches from DateTimePaginator to OptimizedCursorPaginator while still passing order_by="-datetime". OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on that field. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first page that contains any rows raises TypeError while building the next/prev cursor. value_from_cursor also returns the raw cursor integer instead of a datetime, so a later page would compare a timestamptz column to an integer and fail in Postgres. The new path is unusable and has no tests; the default path is unchanged.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/ceil to the datetime field used for order_by='-datetime', which raises a TypeError. It also adds further detail about value_from_cursor.

false_positives.candidate:
Eviction is not atomic with insert and can empty a segment

Span payloads are ZADDed in a separate non-transactional pipeline, and add-buffer.lua never receives the payload or score, so it cannot insert them. The 1000-span cap is a later ZPOPMIN using a count observed inside that script. Redis serializes each script, but two writers can both ZADD past the cap and both compute span_count-1000 from the pre-pop size. ProcessSpansStrategyFactory runs process_batch in a multiprocessing pool when num_processes != 1, and those workers share shards; rebalance/spillover can also double-write a trace. Two scripts that each see 2000 members will each pop 1000 and leave the segment empty. The old set-based union did not delete members on insert, so this data loss is new.

Set-to-sorted-set switch breaks existing span-buffer keys

The buffer keys stay span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id, but the script and SpansBuffer now use ZADD, ZCARD, ZUNIONSTORE, ZSCAN, and ZPOPMIN. The previous code stored those keys as Redis SETs (SADD/SCARD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN). There is no new prefix, TYPE check, or migration. After deploy, every live segment is still a set until redis_ttl (default 3600s). ZADD or ZSCAN on it raises WRONGTYPE, process_spans fails, and the consumer retries the same batch for every in-flight trace. Flush fails the same way, so those segments are neither emitted nor deleted until the key expires.

ZUNIONSTORE SUM and self-union UNLINK drop or mis-rank spans

Merges use ZUNIONSTORE with the default AGGREGATE SUM. A member present in both inputs (Kafka redelivery, or the same payload written to both the parent key and a child key) gets its end-timestamp scores added, so it sorts as far in the future and ZPOPMIN evicts other spans instead. If the resolved set id equals the current span id, span_key and set_key are the same key: the script unions the key with itself and then UNLINK span_key, deleting the destination the preceding ZADD just wrote. That hits a non-root span whose parent_span_id equals its span_id, or whose redirect chain resolves to its own id. Those spans are gone before flush.

Redirect walk cut from 10000 to 1000 splits deep traces

The parent-redirect loop now stops after 1000 hops, and the comment that this limit fails to join deep segment trees was removed. On a longer chain the loop exits at an intermediate span id, then HSET persists that partial redirect (span_id -> set_span_id). Later spans follow the truncated mapping, so the segment is permanently split and flushed as incomplete pieces. Child-first arrival stores one hop per ancestor, so a trace nested deeper than 1000 spans hits this. The previous cap was 10000 specifically because of that correctness limit.

Hardcoded eviction can drop the root and the flush guard is gone

The cap is ZPOPMIN of span_count-1000 with a literal 1000. SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (default 1001) is no longer consulted, so that constructor argument does nothing. ZPOPMIN deletes the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores with no exception for the segment root, so a root that ended before a child (clock skew or a longer child) is discarded and the flushed segment has no root span. The flush-time check in _load_segment_data that skipped segments over max_segment_spans and emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded was removed, so if insert-time eviction does not run the consumer loads and publishes the whole segment up to the 10MiB byte limit. Evictions are not metered.

No tests for eviction, score order, or the new paginator

Buffer tests were only updated to supply end_timestamp_precise. Every case still uses four or five spans with the same timestamp, so CI never hits ZPOPMIN, never checks that the oldest spans are removed, never checks that the root is kept, and never covers WRONGTYPE on existing set keys or the concurrent double-pop race. The new audit-log OptimizedCursorPaginator path also has no test, so the datetime TypeError and the negative-offset ValueError would not fail CI.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Eligibility cache key uses process-randomized hash() and cannot be invalidated

The cache key is error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}. Python hash() is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so workers do not share keys, invalidate_upsampling_cache deletes a different key than other processes wrote, and nothing in this PR calls that invalidator when the allowlist changes anyway. A collision of two project-id tuples in one process also serves the wrong eligibility for 60 seconds and rewrites count() for projects that are not fully allowlisted. Use a stable key (for example a sorted, joined id list) and hook invalidation to allowlist updates, or drop the cache; options.get is already an in-process read.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate raises the same problem as the golden comment. It says hash() is process-randomized, so the cache keys differ across workers and invalidation fails. It also proposes the same fix: a stable, deterministic key.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling decision ignores the dataset and query actually executed

_get_event_stats decides upsampling from the closed-over request dataset and request.GET, not from scoped_dataset or the query argument. Dashboard widget splitting calls this helper with a different dataset and rewritten queries (errors-only "!event.type:transaction", transactions-only "event.type:transaction", and the original metrics dataset). A metrics/discover split therefore either skips upsampling on the errors subquery (outer dataset is not errors/discover) or, when the original request string looks like an error query, applies sum(sample_weight) to the transactions-only probe. Split detection uses those counts (has_errors / has_transactions), so widget discoverSplitDecision can be saved incorrectly, and transaction probes can throw if sample_weight is absent. The eligibility check has to use the dataset and query string passed into this call.
true_positives.reasoning: Both say the upsampling eligibility check uses the outer/closed-over dataset rather than scoped_dataset, so upsampling is skipped in dashboard split paths. The candidate adds detail about the query string, but the core issue is the same.

false_positives.candidate:
Allowlist option is never registered and is read on every stats query

Every events-stats execution calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, which on a cache miss calls options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", []). This PR never registers that option (no defaults.py or options change). Sentry's options manager raises UnknownOption for unregistered keys even when a default is passed, so a cache miss 500s the whole organization events-stats endpoint, including non-error datasets and projects that should not be upsampled. If a deployment's options.get instead returns the default, the feature never turns on in production; the new tests hide that by mocking options. The lookup also does `project_id in allowlist` with no int/str normalization, so a JSON allowlist of string ids never matches int project ids (feature silently off), and a non-list value raises TypeError on this same hot path.

count() is rewritten to a column string the field parser will not accept

When upsampling is enabled, count() is replaced with the literal "upsampled_count() as count" and passed as a selected column / y-axis. Sentry's field parser treats a column as a function only when the string ends with ')'; this value does not, so it is resolved as a raw column name rather than the new upsampled_count aggregate. Allowlisted error count() stats queries then fail field validation (or, if an alias were accepted, the result key would not stay the `count` field the events-stats contract and the new test expect). Charts, top-events, and any client requesting yAxis=count() for an allowlisted project break instead of returning an upsampled series.

Upsampled count sums sample_weight, but nothing stores the inverse sample rate

upsampled_count is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no ifNull/coalesce. The only write-path change is the test factory, which copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate onto sample_rate (the rate itself, e.g. 0.1), not sample_weight, and production ingest is not updated at all. Events therefore have no sample_weight. ClickHouse sum of nulls is 0, so once the rewrite runs, allowlisted error counts become 0 instead of the real count or 1/sample_rate. That also cannot satisfy the new stats test, which stores client_sample_rate 0.1 and expects count == 10. toInt64 additionally truncates any fractional weight. Historical events and transactions that lack the column are zeroed or fail the query rather than falling back to count().

The list view now computes canPause and canDelete from Grafana Prometheus abilities, but the menu still renders Pause only when rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) is true (line 123) and Delete only when rulerRule is set (line 165). GrafanaRuleListItem and FilterView pass only promRule, so both items stay hidden even for users who are allowed to pause or delete. Those actions are gone from the new alert list; GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx locks this in by expecting exactly four menu items and never asserting Delete or Pause.

skipToken still grants Duplicate via Grafana create permission

useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(skipToken) evaluates useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) instead of returning all-denied abilities. With no rule, loading is false, so MaybeSupported is AlwaysSupported and Duplicate is allowed whenever the user has Grafana AlertingRuleCreate. AlertRuleMenu ORs that result with the ruler result, so cloud and ruler-only rules show Duplicate for anyone who can create Grafana rules, even when the datasource ability denies it. Update and Delete do not leak because their allowed flag stays false, but Duplicate does.

Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable

useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to set isFederated from isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) and block update, delete, pause, restore, and permanent delete. It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated to false (TODO on line 243). Every caller of useAlertRuleAbility, including the existing rules UI, will offer edit and delete on Mimir/enterprise federated groups. groupIdentifier does not carry source_tenants, so the check was dropped rather than moved.

Rule links no longer include returnTo

The removed GrafanaRuleListItem built the view href with createReturnTo() so the rule detail back link returned to the current list, including filters. The new href is only /alerting/grafana/${uid}/view. Opening a rule from the list and using the in-app back control drops the user on the default alerting page instead of the filtered list.

Prometheus abilities treat only alerting rules as exportable

useAllRulerRuleAbilities allows ModifyExport, Pause, Restore, and DeletePermanently for any Grafana-managed rule (alerting or recording) via rulerRuleType.grafana.rule. useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates those same actions on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule. The list view relies on the Prometheus hook, so Grafana recording rules lose Export (and would also lose pause/restore/permanent delete once those menu items no longer require a ruler rule).

Creating and deleting rules are no longer distinguished

GrafanaGroupLoader used to match ruler and Prometheus rules and render ruler-only rules as Creating and Prometheus-only rules as Deleting (without edit or more actions). It now lists only Prometheus rules. Until Prometheus catches up, a just-created rule is missing from the group, and a just-deleted rule still appears as a normal rule with edit, silence, duplicate, and export. The tests that covered those states were removed rather than replaced.

isProvisionedPromRule reads provenance on a type that lacks it

isProvisionedPromRule takes PromRuleDTO and accesses promRule.provenance after prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule). That helper is not a type predicate, and PromRuleDTO (PromAlertingRuleDTO | PromRecordingRuleDTO) does not declare provenance — only GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase does. This is a TypeScript error, and RuleActionsButtons passes a Rule into this function, so provisioned detection for the clone flow may not typecheck. At runtime a non-Grafana rule short-circuits, but a Grafana rule is only treated as provisioned if the object happens to have provenance.

Early interpolation defeats the $__range split exclusion

runSplitQuery now runs every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables before querySupportsSplitting. That helper replaces Grafana range macros ($__range, $__range_s, $__range_ms) from request.scopedVars using the full request range. querySupportsSplitting then calls isQueryWithRangeVariable on the already-rewritten expr, so the $__range token is gone and the query is treated as splittable. The comment on querySupportsSplitting says these queries must not be split because the macro is meant to be interpolated on the backend against each request's own time range. After this change each chunk is executed with the full-range duration baked in (for example count_over_time({app="x"}[7d]) on every 1-day slice), so merged results overlap or over-count and Loki load grows with the selected range. The new tests only cover $__auto and $step, and the default test templateSrv does not expand $__range, so this production path is untested. Interpolate only after classifying queries on the raw expr, and leave $__range* in the expression sent to the backend.

Shard queries are template-interpolated twice, including ad-hoc filters

runShardSplitQuery now maps every target through applyTemplateVariables(query, scopedVars, request.filters), then splitQueriesByStreamShard rewrites those expressions with interpolateShardingSelector and calls runSplitQuery. runSplitQuery unconditionally applies applyTemplateVariables again on that rewritten expr, with the same request.filters still set. applyTemplateVariables is not idempotent: ad-hoc filters are inserted into the stream selector on each call, so a sharded query gets duplicate matchers (or a failed/misplaced insertion once `| drop __stream_shard__` is already in the LogQL). A second template replace can also expand `$` sequences that appeared in variable values. The updated shard test expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times for a single target (once here plus once per split group) and only uses an idempotent replace mock, so it locks in the double application instead of catching duplicate filters. Interpolate once, before shard selector injection, and do not run applyTemplateVariables again inside runSplitQuery for targets that are already interpolated.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Device limit check is not atomic with the insert

CreateOrUpdateDevice counts rows in one session, then inserts in another, with no transaction, row lock, or unique cap. Concurrent anonymous logins that all observe count < deviceLimit all take the INSERT path and the table (and thus anonymous access) exceeds the configured limit. This is the common case when many new devices arrive together at the cap. The count and the insert/update need to be serialized (single transaction with a lock, or an insert that rechecks the cap) so the limit cannot be overrun.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same race condition: the device count check and the insert are not atomic, so concurrent requests can exceed the limit. Both suggest a transaction or lock as the fix.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Device-limit denial is cached as success

tagDeviceUI writes the device key into the 29-minute local cache before CreateOrUpdateDevice returns. On ErrDeviceLimitReached the first call correctly fails, but the cache entry is left in place and the next TagDevice for that same X-Grafana-Device-Id hits the cache and returns nil. Authenticate treats nil as success, so anonymous access is granted and the device is never recorded. A client that retries once (or any later request within the TTL) bypasses the limit entirely. The cache is also not cleared on transient DB errors, so a failed write is treated as tagged and is not retried for 29 minutes. Set the cache only after a successful write, and do not treat a limit failure as a cache hit.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate describes the same issue. The cache is populated before CreateOrUpdateDevice, it stays set on ErrDeviceLimitReached, and later requests bypass the device limit for the 29-minute TTL.

false_positives.candidate:
Device limit is enforced only if the client sends a device id

The new auth denial depends on TagDevice, which returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is missing, and Authenticate then issues an anonymous identity. The header is optional and client-controlled, so omitting it never consumes a slot and never hits ErrDeviceLimitReached. A caller can also mint device_limit distinct ids to fill the quota (locking out honest frontends that do send the header) and then drop the header to keep its own anonymous access. As written, the limit cannot cap anonymous access. Enforcement needs a server-issued identifier, or requests without a tracked device must be denied once the cap is reached.

Provider signature change will not compile with existing wire code

ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer accepts anonstore.AnonStore and now requires db.DB, and ProvideAnonDBStore gained a deviceLimit parameter. This package is constructed by the committed Wire injector (pkg/server/wire_gen.go), which is not updated in this PR and still calls the old signatures. The server build fails until wire is regenerated. Any other in-repo or enterprise caller that passed an AnonStore is also broken, and tests can no longer inject a fake store.

Device-limit failure is returned as an unclassified error

When the cap is hit, Authenticate returns the raw anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached sentinel (a plain fmt.Errorf). That is not an errutil or authn error, so the auth middleware treats it as an unexpected failure and typically responds with HTTP 500 rather than a controlled 401/403 and a user-facing device-limit message. It also shows up as a server error in logs. Return a typed unauthorized/forbidden auth error so the client chain and HTTP layer handle it as an access denial.

Limit tests miss the allow-existing path and auth enforcement

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only inserts a second, unknown device id against the store and expects ErrDeviceLimitReached. It never checks that a device already inside the 30-day window can still be updated once the cap is reached, and nothing covers TagDevice, the local cache, or Anonymous.Authenticate. Those are the paths that actually grant or deny access, so the cache-as-success bypass and the missing-header bypass are untested and would ship green.

device_limit is not added to default config

auth.anonymous.device_limit is read with MustInt64(0), but conf/defaults.ini (and the docs generated from it) are not updated. Operators have no documented default, comment, or sample for the new cap, and 0-means-unlimited exists only in the store's if deviceLimit > 0 check. Add the key to the [auth.anonymous] section in defaults.ini with that meaning spelled out.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

false_positives.candidate:
Translation path never loads fallback locale files

I18n.translate still only calls load_locale for config.locale, and the new ensure_loaded! helper is invoked only from ApplicationController#set_locale. The accelerator otherwise refuses to load YAML except for that one locale, while I18n::Backend::Fallbacks looks up SiteSetting.default_locale and :en in memory. Jobs, mailers, I18n.with_locale, and any I18n.t outside that before_filter therefore miss fallback strings (and plural rules) that exist on disk. Calls with no interpolation args then freeze the "translation missing" result in the LRU cache, so later loading the fallback locale does not repair that key until restart or eviction.

Cached translations ignore the fallback locale

The no-argument translation cache key is only the key, I18n.locale, and backend object id. FallbackLocaleList now resolves missing keys through SiteSetting.default_locale, which admins can change at runtime without I18n.reload!. A string that was filled from the old site locale stays cached under the user locale, so after a default-locale change users of incomplete locales keep seeing the previous language for hot keys until process restart or LRU eviction.

Fallbacks turned on in development and test

config.i18n.fallbacks = true was previously limited to production, profile, and the cloud66 production file, so development and test left missing keys visible. This initializer always includes I18n::Backend::Fallbacks and installs FallbackLocaleList, with no environment guard. In development and test, a key missing from the current locale now silently becomes the site-locale or English string instead of the missing-translation marker, which hides incomplete locale files and can change specs that set a non-English locale and assert on missing keys or exact untranslated output.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host allow-list lookup ignores case and port

Lookup is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` using `URI#host` unchanged. The column side is lowercased but the bind value is not, so a referer host `Example.com` does not match a saved `example.com` under PostgreSQL. The format validator explicitly allows `:port`, and `before_validation` keeps it, but `URI#host` never includes the port, so a saved host `example.com:3000` never matches `http://example.com:3000/...`. Those referers are rejected by `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes unless embed_category matches a category name

The migration always runs `execute(... embed_category ...)[0]['id']`. Discourse only persists site settings that were overridden, and the join is `site_settings.value = categories.name`. On a normal install embed_category is absent or blank, the result set is empty, and `[0]` is nil, so the migration raises NoMethodError. PostgreSQL rolls the transaction back, so the upgrade cannot complete and embedding cannot be moved off the old setting.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the migration indexing [0]['id'] on an empty result when no embed_category setting or matching category exists, which causes a crash. This is the same issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Existing allow-list is deleted and never copied

The copy of `embeddable_hosts` is gated on `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` after a SELECT. PG::Result#cmd_tuples is 0 for SELECT (row count is `ntuples`). The INSERT loop never runs, then the migration deletes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings. Any site that gets past the category lookup loses its allow-list and embedding starts rejecting every referer.

Import passes a category id through the name option

PostCreator is still called with `category:`, which previously received `SiteSetting.embed_category`, a category name (the migration joins that setting to `categories.name`). The new code passes `eh.try(:category_id)`, an integer. Nothing in this PR teaches PostCreator to treat that option as an id, so embedded topic creation will either raise or land in the uncategorized category instead of the host's chosen category. The new expectation in topic_embed_spec does not change PostCreator.

Hosts are not unique, so category assignment is arbitrary

There is no uniqueness validation and the migration adds no unique index on `host`. `record_for_host` uses `.first` with no order. Two rows for the same host (easy via the admin API, or a re-run of a fixed migration) make embed imports pick an arbitrary category, so "post to category" is not stable.

Plural id hydration throws when the ids value is null

The new `*_ids` branch always calls `obj[k].map(...)` and only then does `hydrated || []`. A rest payload with a null or missing array for any `*_ids` key (not just embeddable hosts) throws TypeError inside `_hydrate` and fails the whole `find`/`findAll`. The `|| []` never runs for null, and the ids key is deleted only after the map.

New embed admin API and migration are untested

The new controller specs only assert the class subclasses AdminController. They never hit create, update, destroy, a missing id, a blank host, or an unknown category. There is also no migration spec, so the empty `embed_category` crash, the `cmd_tuples` data loss, and un-normalized host inserts are not caught. `topic_spec`'s "embeddable_host is blank" example no longer stubs a host or an embed, so it does not lock the new `expandable_first_post?` behavior either.

It should keep 30% of `$primary` for light and use 70% of `$secondary` for dark, matching the transform applied to other 30% primary colors.

Mobile topic-map heading lightness changed from 20% to 50%

`.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. It is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which is the h4 color copied onto the heading. The desktop rule for the same heading correctly keeps 20% of `$primary` and uses 80% of `$secondary`. On mobile, light-theme topic-map headings become lighter than before, and dark-theme headings do not match the desktop complement, so the heading is no longer darker/stronger than the h4 beneath it.

Category badge notification color still scales $primary only

In the same file whose topic-list header, cell, excerpt, and education colors were wrapped in `dark-light-choose`, `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still sets `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. On a dark theme `$primary` is already near white, so raising its lightness makes this transparent-background notification text nearly the same as primary text instead of the muted gray used by the neighboring list colors. It should follow the same 50% `$primary` / 50% `$secondary` pair used for the other 50% text colors in this file.

true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
totalPages is off by one when count is a multiple of page size

totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is wrong whenever user_count is greater than 0 and divisible by limit. A group of exactly 50 members with the default limit of 50 is reported as 2 pages, 100 members as 3, and so on. showingLast compares currentPage to that value, so Next stays enabled on the last real page. next() then sets offset to min(offset + limit, user_count), which equals user_count, and findMembers loads an empty page. Admins see a blank extra page and a wrong "N/M" indicator for every full page of members.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: when user_count is a multiple of limit, next sets offset to user_count, which yields an empty last page with a wrong indicator such as 2/2. The candidate attributes it to the totalPages calculation, but it describes the same scenario and also mentions the next() cap.

true_positives.golden_comment: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
No coverage for alias level or the new members payload

The create example only posts a name and asserts stripping. Nothing asserts that alias_level from the flat params is persisted, which is the field create now ignores. There is also no spec for GroupsController#members, so the new {members, meta} contract, the default page size, and unbounded limit/offset are untested. The automatic remove example calls xhr :put, :remove_member while the route is DELETE; controller specs still invoke the action, so that mismatch does not fail CI and does not lock the route param (:group_id) either.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate mainly covers missing test coverage, but it also says the remove example calls xhr :put on remove_member while the route is DELETE. That is the same mismatch the golden comment describes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
totalPages is off by one when count is a multiple of page size

totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is wrong whenever user_count is greater than 0 and divisible by limit. A group of exactly 50 members with the default limit of 50 is reported as 2 pages, 100 members as 3, and so on. showingLast compares currentPage to that value, so Next stays enabled on the last real page. next() then sets offset to min(offset + limit, user_count), which equals user_count, and findMembers loads an empty page. Admins see a blank extra page and a wrong "N/M" indicator for every full page of members.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same bug: the Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 totalPages formula adds an extra page when the count is an exact multiple of the limit, which lets users navigate to an empty page.

false_positives.candidate:
Public group members page only loads the first 50 users

setupController always calls Group.findMembers(), and that method now always requests limit 50 (the new model default) and offset 0. The public members template (group/members.hbs) only iterates `members` and has no next/previous controls, unlike the admin group screen. Previously this endpoint returned every member of a non-automatic group and defaulted automatic groups to 200 when no limit was sent. After this change, any group with more than 50 members (including large custom groups and automatic groups such as trust_level_0) silently hides everyone past the first page, with no way to load the rest.

Removing the last member on a page leaves a blank page

findMembers clamps the request offset with Math.min(user_count, offset) using the in-memory user_count, which is only refreshed from the response. removeMember (and addMembers) then call findMembers() without moving offset back. Deleting the last user on the current page therefore re-requests an offset that is now past the end (the clamp still allows offset == old total). The server echoes that offset in meta and returns an empty members array, and the client stores meta.offset, so the admin UI stays on a blank page until Previous is clicked. The members action never clamps offset to the last non-empty page either.

Remove control ignores whether the group is automatic

This row is rendered by the group-member itemView, not in the admin group template's context. Ember's each+itemView sets the row context to the each keyword ({member: user}) or to the user record; neither has the group's automatic flag, and a replaced context does not fall back to the admin-group controller. {{#unless automatic}} is therefore always true, so the remove link is shown for automatic groups (admins, moderators, trust_level_*, and so on). Confirming still calls DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members, which correctly returns 422, but neither the removeMember action nor Group.removeMember handles the failure, so the admin gets a confirm dialog and then no error and no list refresh.

Creating a group drops the chosen alias level

create assigns name and visible, then saves, but never reads params[:alias_level]. The admin form shows the alias-level combo for new groups (it sits outside the {{#if id}} block), and Group.asJSON posts alias_level on create. update does apply alias_level, so editing an existing group works, but the first save always persists the default (0, nobody) no matter what was selected. The client only copies resp.basic_group.id back onto the model, so the UI keeps showing the unsaved choice until the group is reloaded. The new create spec only checks name stripping and would not catch this.

Members limit and offset are unbounded and can 500

The rewritten members action uses limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset = params[:offset].to_i with no upper or lower bound. This route is available to anyone who can see the group, including public automatic groups that contain every user. A very large limit loads and serializes the entire membership in one request. A negative offset or limit is sent through to SQL; PostgreSQL rejects OFFSET/LIMIT < 0, so those query params 500 the endpoint. The old action at least defaulted automatic groups to 200; the rewrite should cap limit (and reject negative offset/limit) rather than trusting the client.

GET /groups/:name/members.json response shape changed

members used to render_serialized an array of GroupUserSerializer objects. It now returns an object {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}. The in-repo Group.findMembers caller was updated, but this is a public route. Themes, plugins, and API clients that treated the body as an array (for example result.map or a JSON array decode) will break or show no members. There is no compat path, such as keeping the array when limit/offset are omitted, or a versioned response.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Match stats are written inside validation and rolled back or double-counted

should_block? is invoked from EmailValidator during User validation, but it is not a pure check: it does match_count += 1, sets last_match_at, and calls save. User#save runs validations inside a transaction and raises ActiveRecord::Rollback when the user is invalid, so the counter update made while rejecting a blocked address is undone and never persisted on a normal save/save!/create. UsersController#create hides this for one path only: it calls user.valid? first (that increment commits) and then user.save (a second increment that rolls back), so the count is right there only by accident and any extra valid? double-counts. The same read-modify-write save also writes every column, so two concurrent matches can lose increments and a concurrent admin change to action_type can be overwritten. Match auditing is unreliable, and the new specs only call should_block? directly so they never catch the rollback.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same problem: the should_block? check has side effects, because it increments match stats and saves during what should be a read operation. The candidate also covers race conditions, which the golden comment raises too. It adds extra detail about rollback and double-counting, but the core issue is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored

email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) after only escaping dots, then uses =~ with no end anchor or domain boundary. A whitelist value of company.com therefore matches user@company.com.attacker.example (and user@company.com.extra) as well as user@company.com, so a site that restricts signup to specific providers can be bypassed by any domain that merely contains the allowed domain as a substring. The same pattern makes a blacklist over-match unrelated hosts such as user@spam.com.legitimate.example. This is now the only server-side domain check (it was moved here from User), and nothing in the new specs covers whitelist or blacklist behavior.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same flaw: the regex @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? lacks proper anchoring or boundaries, which lets the domain whitelist be bypassed. The golden comment gives a subdomain example (evil.example.com), while the candidate gives a trailing-suffix example (company.com.attacker.example). The examples differ, but the underlying regex anchoring bug is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email check is case- and whitespace-sensitive

BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the address with an exact BlockedEmail.where(email: email) match, and BlockedEmail only validates uniqueness of the raw email string (no downcasing or stripping in set_defaults). Signup stores whatever the user typed (User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] unchanged), while other paths such as change_email normalize with Email.downcase and strip. A blocked row for "bad@spam.com" therefore does not match "Bad@spam.com" or "bad@spam.com ", and the case-sensitive unique index will not treat those as the same address. Someone who was blocked can still register by changing case or surrounding whitespace.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same flaw: the email lookup in BlockedEmail.should_block? is case-sensitive, so a blocked address can be bypassed by changing its case. The candidate also mentions whitespace, but the core issue is identical.

true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
2009 box display prefixes drop the header float fallback

flexbox() emits display: -webkit-box and display: -moz-box (and inline-flex() emits the inline equivalents) before the 2012 and unprefixed values. Engines that only implement the 2009 box model will honor that display and ignore later ones. That model does not pack with margin-left: auto and ignores float on children, but this PR removed .d-header .title { float: left } and .panel { float: right } and now depends on margin-left: auto to keep login and notification controls on the right. Those browsers therefore lay the logo and the panel out together at the start. Engines that understand none of the prefixed display values also lose the float fallback, so .panel becomes a normal full-width block under the logo. Either omit the 2009 display values and keep the floats as the non-flex fallback, or implement the matching -webkit-box-pack / -webkit-box-flex rules; the prefixes as written do not reproduce the layout they replaced.
true_positives.reasoning: Both flag that removing the .panel float-right fallback causes the panel to lose right alignment and stack under the title. The candidate attributes this to old or non-flex browsers rather than the noscript non-flex-item structure, but it targets the same code change and the same symptom.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
box-ordinal-group is not shifted to the 1-based scale

@mixin order writes $val unchanged to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. Those 2009 properties are 1-based (initial value 1) and reject non-positive integers, while order, -webkit-order, and -ms-flex-order are 0-based (initial value 0). The equivalent legacy value is $val + 1. Today's call sites pass 2 and 3, so they still sort after items that omit order (legacy groups 1, 2, 3 versus modern 0, 2, 3) and the header does not mis-order yet. The shared mixin is still wrong for the model it claims to support: order(1) ties with unstyled siblings instead of following them, and order(0) is an invalid ordinal so the declaration is dropped and the item stays in the default group.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same bug. The legacy -webkit/-moz-box-ordinal-group properties are 1-based, but the mixin passes $val through unchanged. As a result, a value of 0 is invalid and items are ordered incorrectly in older browsers.

false_positives.candidate:
Small-action button float is ignored inside the new flex row

.small-action is now a flex container (flexbox() and align-items(center) at lines 264-265), but the action button is still placed with float: right. Float does not apply to flex items, and the patch never replaces it with margin-left: auto on the button or flex: 1 on .small-action-desc. For the usual short small-action label (closed, pinned, archived) in a wide post, the delete button therefore sits immediately after the text instead of at the right edge, which is where float: right put it. The description's old padding (0.5em 0 0.5em 4em) that cleared the 45px floated avatar was also reduced to 0 1.5%, so any browser that ignores every display value emitted by flexbox() still honors float: left on .topic-avatar and draws the label underneath that icon.

Header flex row overflows and pushes controls off-screen

.d-header .contents is now display: flex with the default flex-wrap: nowrap. .title, .extra-info-wrapper (only order: 2 in topic.scss), and .panel (only margin-left: auto and order: 3) never set min-width: 0, overflow: hidden, or flex-shrink: 0. Flex items default to min-width: auto, so they will not shrink below their content minimum, and margin-left: auto only eats positive free space — it does not stop overflow. A wide site logo (this file only sets #site-logo max-height: 40px, not a max-width) or a long docked topic title plus the 32px header icons therefore overflows the bar instead of ellipsizing or wrapping. On a narrow viewport the fixed header widens the page and login/notification controls are pushed out of view. The old float: left / float: right layout kept the panel shrink-to-fit on the right and let the middle content wrap inside the header width. Give the middle item flex: 1, min-width: 0, and overflow: hidden, and set flex-shrink: 0 on .title and .panel.

false_negatives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is never invoked

ActiveModel::Serializer only calls include_<attr>? (every other hook in this file uses that name). include_website_name has no question mark, so it is dead code and the attribute is always serialized. Users with a blank or unparsable website still get website_name: null in /users/:username.json, and any condition placed in this method will not run.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem as the golden comment: include_website_name lacks the ? suffix, so the serializer never calls it and the attribute is always included. It does not mention the string mutation concern, but the main issue matches.

false_positives.candidate:
website_name bypasses TL0 website hiding

website is listed in untrusted_attributes, so anonymous viewers of a trust-level 0 user do not receive user_profile.website (anti-spam: the profile must not expose a new user's site). website_name is a new public attribute and is not in that list, and its method reads object.user_profile.website directly. Anonymous clients therefore still get the host, and the path whenever the domain heuristic matches, and user.hbs renders that as the globe label. The new specs never serialize a TL0 user with Guardian.new and assert website_name is absent, so this regression is untested.

Same-domain path display is case-sensitive

website_host is taken from URI#host, which keeps the URL's casing, and is compared to Discourse.current_hostname with == and String#ends_with? (both case-sensitive). A site on example.com and a website of http://Example.com/user, or a site on forums.example.com and a website of http://Example.com/user, fails every branch and the profile shows only the host. The feature then does not show the path for ordinary mixed-case links. The specs only stub lowercase hosts.

Domain check mis-classifies hosts and misses www vs apex

The equal-label branch treats any two hosts with the same label count above 2 as the same site when every label but the first matches. On a forum at mysite.github.io or forum.co.uk, http://evil.github.io/phish and http://other.co.uk/phish are therefore rendered with the full path, not just the host. The else branch (discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host)) is true for any dotted suffix, so a website host of com or co.uk is treated as the parent of a normal forum hostname. The check is also asymmetric for the common www case: instance example.com vs website www.example.com/user does not match (label counts differ, and example.com does not end with .www.example.com), so the path is hidden, while instance www.example.com vs website example.com/user does show the path. None of these cases are covered by the new specs.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Resize listener accepts any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl

The check is `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, i.e. accept when the sender origin is any substring of discourseUrl, not when it equals the forum origin. A shorter origin that is a prefix matches: if discourseUrl is `https://discuss.example.com`, a window at `https://discuss.example.co` has index 0 and is accepted. That page can postMessage a `discourse-resize` and set the iframe height arbitrarily (hide comments or stretch the frame over the host page). Compare parsed origins for equality, and require index 0 only if a prefix check is kept.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments say the indexOf-based origin check is inadequate and can be bypassed by a malicious origin. The bypass examples differ. The golden comment uses a domain like evil-discourseUrl.com, while the candidate uses a prefix/substring origin. The underlying flaw, insecure origin validation via indexOf, is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage targetOrigin is the full referer, so resize is dropped

The embed layout calls `parent.postMessage(..., request.referer)`. postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`), not a full URL with path and query. Browsers drop the message (or throw) when it does not match the parent origin. embed.js also sets the iframe to `scrolling=no` and only grows it on `discourse-resize`, so the comments frame stays at the default height and clips the discussion. Pass the referer origin only (and escape it for the JS string).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate points to the same issue: postMessage targetOrigin is set to the full referer URL instead of the origin, so the message is dropped and the resize never happens.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
raw_html cook path stores and serves unsanitized HTML

Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, skipping PrettyText and Discourse's sanitizer. TopicEmbed.import persists RSS/Readability HTML with that cook method, and the embed view prints it with `raw post.cooked` (the main topic UI also treats cooked as HTML). PollFeed does `CGI.unescapeHTML` on feed content first, so entity-encoded markup becomes live tags, and Readability's allow-list still permits `javascript:`/`data:` href and src. Any feed item or fetched page can therefore plant stored XSS that runs for every forum visitor, not just inside the embed iframe. The imported-from footer makes this worse by interpolating the URL into an href with no escaping (`<a href='#{url}'>` in TopicEmbed.import), so a quote in an otherwise allowed http(s) URL breaks out of the attribute.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment raises two issues: a NoMethodError when contents is nil, and XSS from the unescaped url interpolation. The candidate explicitly covers the second, the unescaped url interpolated into the href in TopicEmbed.import. It does not mention the nil contents case, but it does match a core part of the golden issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embed template has invalid ERB (`end if`)

`<%- end if %>` compiles to the Ruby statement `end if`, which is a SyntaxError. Rendering `/embed/best` when a topic already exists (the success path in EmbedController#best) will raise while compiling the template, so the iframe never shows highlights. It must be `<% end %>`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the invalid `end if` in the ERB template, note that it raises an error at render time, and recommend replacing it with a plain `end`. They describe the same issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed poll crashes unless every item has string content

`i.content.scrub` assumes every SimpleRSS item has a String `content`. RSS 2.0 items typically expose `description` and leave `content` nil; Atom can also omit it. Nil (or a non-string) raises NoMethodError, and because there is no rescue the hourly job aborts before later items are imported. `String#scrub` is also Ruby 2.1+ only, so this line fails on Ruby 2.0 even when content is present. Use description/content fallback and guard nil before unescaping.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate points to the same problem as the golden comment. `i.content.scrub` fails when `content` is nil because many RSS items provide only `description`. Both recommend falling back to `description`. The candidate's extra notes, such as Ruby version support, don't change that the core issue is the same.

false_positives.candidate:
Unauthenticated embed URL fetch is an SSRF and topic-spam vector

import_remote uses `open(url).read` (open-uri) with no timeout, size limit, or redirect restriction. EmbedController#best is a public GET whose only gate is `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Referer is client-controlled, so any caller can spoof it and pass `embed_url` on the configured host. TopicRetriever then fetches that URL; open-uri follows redirects to arbitrary hosts (including link-local and cloud metadata). Each miss also enqueues RetrieveTopic with no controller-side dedupe, so unique URLs create unbounded jobs and, on success, topics posted as embed_by_username. open-uri is not even required from this file, so the fetch only works if some other file has already patched Kernel#open.

Embed controller spec expects a sync retrieve the action does not do

The 'no previous embed' example expects `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` during `get :best`. EmbedController#best only calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, so mocha fails this example and the job/throttle path is untested. The other success example renders `embed/best`, which currently raises SyntaxError on `end if`, so the `response.should be_success` after-hook fails as well. The spec will not pass as written and does not lock in the async behavior.

Disqus import drops category, original date, and offline permalinks

The importer no longer accepts `--category` and no longer passes `created_at` or `category` into topic creation. It now depends on `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which HTTP-fetches `t[:link]` and returns nil on any network/HTTP error. The following comment import is skipped entirely when that fetch fails, so a dead or blocked article URL drops the whole Disqus thread instead of creating the previous permalink stub. Category placement and original thread timestamps are also lost, and a single failed fetch aborts the rest of the file because nothing rescues `open`.

embed_url is varchar(255) but used as the unique lookup key

`t.string :embed_url` is a 255-character varchar, with a unique index on that column. TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed and import look up the full URL. Article and RSS links with tracking query strings routinely exceed 255 characters, so insert raises and the topic is never associated; truncated values would also collide or miss on lookup. Store embed_url as text (and index a hash if a unique constraint is still required).

content_sha1 is advanced even when the post is not updated

On change, import always calls `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` after `revise!`, without checking that revise!/save succeeded. PostRevisor#revise! returns false when raw is unchanged and still returns true if `save` fails; either way the SHA is overwritten. The next poll then treats the feed item as already imported and never retries, so the topic body stays stale. If the linked post was deleted, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(post)` raises, which aborts the rest of the feed run. Update the SHA only after a successful save, and skip or recreate when the post is gone.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition overwrites the width/height API

Ruby does not overload by arity, so downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) on line 149 replaces downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) on line 145. The width/height wrapper never exists at runtime. Callers that still use the previous signature — numeric max width and max height, which this pull request does not update anywhere else — now bind the height integer to opts. optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] and raises NoMethodError instead of building a widthxheight geometry, so those calls 500.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:

The new working-hours test uses Array.find and returns unavailable if the slot falls outside any single window whose days include the slot's UTC weekday. A host with a lunch break, or a single local range that getWorkingHours splits across UTC midnight into two entries on the same day, therefore fails the check for every slot: a 10:00 slot inside 09:00–12:00 is still outside 13:00–17:00, so find matches and the slot is dropped. The booking page then shows no times. The condition is also inverted for days off: if no window lists that weekday, find matches nothing and the host is treated as free, so a fixed host who does not work that day is not actually blocked. It does still explicitly say the end minute is copied from slotStartTime instead of slot end, which lets slots that overrun endTime through. That is the same issue as the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

A fixed host (including every personal or collective host) who blocked 15:00 with a calendar event or Cal booking, but has a date override covering that time, is reported free, so the slot stays bookable and can double-book. The same find() treats "outside this one override" as a hard unavailable: two override windows on the same day reject a slot that sits in only one of them, because the other window's callback returns true. Zero-length overrides (the unavailable-day convention, start equal to end) are detected with dayjs object ===, which is never true for two instances, so that branch never runs. Day matching compares dayjs(date.start).add(offset).format (process-local mode) to slotStartTime.format (UTC mode), so when the server TZ is not UTC the override is attached to the wrong calendar day or ignored. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it is not treated as outside, so it takes the early available return as well.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate raises several issues. One of them says zero-length overrides are detected with dayjs object ===, which is never true for two instances. That is the same issue as the golden comment.

The shifted clock time is then reduced with .hour() and .minute() only. Adding inviteeOffset-organizerOffset across midnight wraps to 0–24h on the unadjusted day (the activeOverrides filter still keys off the raw UTC start). When the wrapped end is less than the wrapped start, buildSlots drops the range (start >= end), so the override disappears. Attendees in a distant timezone see the override on the wrong date or not at all — the bug this change is meant to fix.

No test covers fixed-host overrides or the new availability recheck

The only new test re-queries a personal event date override in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC instants as the IST case. It never builds a round-robin event with a fixed host, which is the main fix described in the PR, and it never hits checkIfIsAvailable's date-override or working-hours branches. Split working hours, an override day that also has a booking, an unavailable (start==end) override, and a timezone shift that crosses midnight are all untested, so the regressions above would merge green.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The handler loops every due reminder with several queries and a Twilio call, and it is a cron POST that can be invoked again if the previous run is still going or the scheduler retries a timeout. Two runs read the same count, both can call scheduleSMS for the same unscheduled row, and both write the same retryCount, so the retryCount > 1 delete never observes the real number of attempts and does not stop duplicate sends. Use retryCount: { increment: 1 } and claim the row before calling Twilio so a second run cannot schedule it again.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same problem. The update sets retryCount to the in-memory reminder.retryCount + 1, which is not atomic and can lose increments under concurrency, and this applies to the catch block as well. Both recommend using Prisma's increment: 1.

This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

A scheduled SMS loses its referenceId without cancelling the provider message, so the text can still go out and can no longer be tracked or cancelled. The retryCount > 1 branch of the deleteMany OR clause has no method SMS filter, so Email and WhatsApp reminders get deleted. The extra points the candidate raises go beyond the golden comment but do not change the core issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Broad catch burns the two-strike limit and can duplicate SMS

The catch surrounds template building, the organizer profile lookup, getBookerBaseUrl, twilio.scheduleSMS, and the success update that sets scheduled and referenceId. Any throw increments retryCount and leaves scheduled false. If Twilio already accepted the message and only the following update failed, the SID is discarded and the next cron calls scheduleSMS again, sending a duplicate; after two such errors retryCount is 2 and the opening deleteMany removes the row while those provider messages stay queued. The same path treats transient failures (DB blip, booker URL, empty attendees) as permanent send failures. This cron loads every unscheduled SMS in the next 7 days, so two errored passes delete that whole backlog and those bookings never get an SMS. Only count a retry when the provider rejects the send, and if scheduleSMS already returned a SID, persist that SID instead of incrementing.

Missing number or empty body is retried until the send date

retryCount is incremented only when message is non-empty and sendTo is set, and only if scheduleSMS returns a falsy value or throws. If the step has no sendTo, the booking has no smsReminderNumber, or the rendered body is empty, the loop just continues. The row stays scheduled false with retryCount 0 and is selected again on every cron run until scheduledDate is in the past, which is the unbounded reschedule this PR is meant to stop (invalid or missing phone). deleteMany now ORs retryCount > 1 onto the cleanup, but WorkflowReminder only indexes (method, scheduled, scheduledDate), (bookingUid), (workflowStepId), (seatReferenceId), and (cancelled, scheduledDate). The new column in schema.prisma has no index. Postgres cannot serve that OR branch from the existing composite index, so every cron run can sequentially scan WorkflowReminder before any SMS is scheduled. That table grows with bookings; a slow cleanup makes this endpoint more likely to overlap the next cron tick.

This change deletes reminder rows and stops SMS after a small number of failures, and nothing in the PR covers that contract. Needed cases: one failure leaves the row and a second failure makes the next run delete it; the gt: 1 cutoff matches "failed twice" and does not allow a third scheduleSMS call; EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows with any retryCount are not deleted; a falsy scheduleSMS result and a thrown provider error both increment; empty sendTo or an empty body does not get reselected until the date; a successful schedule does not increment and is not deleted while still in the future. Without those, the unscoped OR and the two-strike catch can drop or duplicate reminders unnoticed.
